method: Seven read-only auditors (A-G) each took a region of the specification (A-F) or the proto's REQUIRED fields (G) and recorded every RFC 2119 statement with the code and tests they opened. Their entries are model output: the ones this branch changed (changed_by) were re-verified by reproducing the defect and showing the new test fail without the fix; the rest are recorded as found and have not been independently re-verified.

entries.requirement: A generated JSON artifact (`spec/a2a.json`...) MAY be published for convenience to tooling and the website
entries.notes: Concerns the spec project's documentation build, not an SDK.

entries.requirement: SDK language bindings, schemas, and any other derived forms MUST be regenerated from the proto (directly or via code generation) rather than edited manually.
entries.notes: Only the prost message types (feature `proto`, build.rs) are generated from a2a.proto; the primary public serde types (Task, Message, TaskListResponse, AgentCard ...) are hand-written structs, guarded by golden fixtures/proptests rather than generated. proto_schema_sync only checks the .proto copies are byte-identical, not that the Rust types match them.

entries.requirement: Migration guidance MUST be provided via an ancillary document when introducing major breaking changes.
entries.notes: Binds the specification maintainers.

entries.requirement: Legacy documentation anchors MUST be preserved (as hidden HTML anchors) to avoid breaking inbound links.
entries.notes: Binds the specification website.

entries.requirement: SDKs and JSON Schemas SHOULD provide deprecated alias types/definitions to maintain backward compatibility.
entries.notes: The two proto-deprecated OAuth flows (implicit, password) are kept so cards declaring them parse, and since 2026-10-11 carry #[deprecated] as the proto fields do. Two compile_fail doctests deny(deprecated) on each variant; removing the attribute makes the doctest compile and fail (shown). No v1.0 field was renamed, so no renamed-field aliases are needed.

entries.requirement: A deprecated name SHOULD NOT be removed earlier than the next major version after introduction of its replacement.
entries.notes: Both deprecated flows remain in the public enum and on the wire (wire_format_password_oauth_flow round-trips one); removal would be a semver-major change, which cargo-semver-checks gates in CI.

entries.requirement: The keywords "MUST", ... are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.
entries.notes: Definitional.

entries.requirement: ContentTypeNotSupportedError: A Media Type provided in the request's message parts is not supported by the agent.
entries.notes: Only enforced when a card declares input modes and only for parts carrying an explicit mediaType; opt-out via allow_undeclared_input_modes.

entries.requirement: UnsupportedOperationError: Messages sent to Tasks that are in a terminal state ... cannot accept further messages.
TaskNotFoundError: The task ID does not exist or is not accessible.
The agent MAY create a new `Task` to process the provided message asynchronously
or MAY return a direct `Message` response for simple interactions.
entries.notes: Non-streaming only: Message returned when the executor emitted a message and nothing task-shaped (a task row is still persisted).

entries.requirement: The operation MUST return immediately with either task information or response message.
entries.notes: Read together with §3.2.2: with returnImmediately=true the Submitted snapshot is returned at once; the default (blocking) mode waits for terminal/interrupted state as §3.2.2 requires.

entries.requirement: Task processing MAY continue asynchronously after the response when a Task is returned.
entries.notes: Background event processor keeps persisting after the response.

entries.requirement: Subsequent events following a `Task` MAY include stream of TaskStatusUpdateEvent and TaskArtifactUpdateEvent objects
UnsupportedOperationError: Streaming is not supported by the agent
entries.notes: SendStreamingMessage against a card whose streaming capability is false or absent answers UnsupportedOperationError (-32004) over JSON-RPC (test added 2026-10-10, shown to fail with the check disabled). No-op when no card is configured; see §8.1 line 1980.

entries.requirement: UnsupportedOperationError: Messages sent to Tasks that are in a terminal state ... cannot accept further messages.
entries.notes: Shared code path with SendMessage (resolve_task_id runs before the streaming split); the test drives streaming=false only.

entries.requirement: ContentTypeNotSupportedError (streaming)
entries.notes: Same validate_send_params path as unary send.

entries.requirement: TaskNotFoundError (streaming)
entries.notes: Shared path; no streaming-specific test.

entries.requirement: The operation MUST establish a streaming connection for real-time updates.
entries.notes: All four bindings consume the same InMemoryQueueReader.

entries.requirement: The stream MUST follow one of these patterns: (1) Message-only stream ... (2) Task lifecycle stream
entries.notes: The executor's first event decides the pattern (InMemoryQueueReader::set_provisional_task): a Message makes a message-only stream, anything else a task stream that begins with the Task.

entries.requirement: Message-only stream: If the agent returns a Message, the stream MUST contain exactly one `Message` object and then close immediately.
entries.notes: Exactly one Message, then the reader returns None; a read dropped while waiting for the first event keeps the decision (cancel-safety test).

entries.requirement: Task lifecycle stream: If the agent returns a Task, the stream MUST begin with the Task object, followed by zero or more TaskStatusUpdateEvent or TaskArtifactUpdateEvent objects.
The stream MUST close when the task reaches a terminal state (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED, REJECTED).
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-12 a reader ends once it has delivered a terminal state (and whatever was queued ahead of it), instead of waiting for the executor to drop its writer; an executor still running, or writing, after its terminal status no longer holds the stream open. The conformance harness reads the raw channel so nothing_after_terminal still sees such writes. The test failed before the change (stream open after 5 s).

entries.requirement: The agent MAY return a `Task` for complex processing with status/artifact updates
or MAY return a `Message` for direct streaming responses without task overhead.
entries.notes: A Message as the executor's first event is streamed as the whole response.

entries.requirement: The implementation MUST provide immediate feedback on progress and intermediate results.
entries.notes: The stream is returned before the executor finishes (the cooperative-executor test returns the stream while the executor waits on a Notify); events are broadcast as written.

entries.requirement: GetTask TaskNotFoundError: The task ID does not exist or is not accessible.
When `includeArtifacts` is false (the default), the artifacts field MUST be omitted entirely from each Task object in the response.
entries.notes: Handler sets task.artifacts = None unless includeArtifacts is true, and serde skips None, so the field is absent. Tested on a task that has an artifact, for includeArtifacts absent and false, at the handler and on the REST wire; shown to fail with the default flipped.

entries.requirement: The `nextPageToken` field MUST always be present in the response.
entries.notes: Field is a plain String with no skip_serializing_if; gRPC follows proto3 default semantics.

entries.requirement: When there are no more results ... the field MUST be set to an empty string ("").
The operation MUST return only tasks visible to the authenticated client
entries.notes: With RequestHandlerBuilder::isolate_tasks_by_caller the authenticated caller's identity selects the store partition (TenantContext::partition), so another caller's task is TaskNotFound like an unknown id and lists hold only the caller's own; the SDK enforces it, the agent author turns it on (off by default: sharing within a tenant stays the default). Shared-access models (roles, groups) map the group to a tenant with a TenantResolver. Before this branch: Visibility is scoped only by tenant, and only when the deployer installs a TenantResolver bound to authentication plus TenantAware* stores; without a resolver the client-supplied tenant (or the shared default partition) is used (`client_tenant.unwrap_or_default()`), and there is no per-principal scoping within a tenant. Hooks: TenantResolver, ServerInterceptor.

entries.requirement: and MUST use cursor-based pagination for performance and consistency.
Tasks MUST be sorted by last update time in descending order.
Implementations MUST implement appropriate authorization scoping to ensure clients can only access authorized tasks.
entries.notes: With RequestHandlerBuilder::isolate_tasks_by_caller the authenticated caller's identity selects the store partition (TenantContext::partition), so another caller's task is TaskNotFound like an unknown id and lists hold only the caller's own; the SDK enforces it, the agent author turns it on (off by default: sharing within a tenant stays the default). Shared-access models (roles, groups) map the group to a tenant with a TenantResolver. Before this branch: SDK supplies tenant-granular scoping (resolver + strict mode + TenantAware stores); per-user authorization within a tenant is left to the agent author's ServerInterceptor. Default build has no scoping at all.

entries.requirement: Implementations MUST return tasks sorted by their status timestamp time in descending order (most recently updated tasks first).
entries.notes: Tasks without a parseable status timestamp fall back to write order.

entries.requirement: TaskNotCancelableError: The task is not in a cancelable state
CancelTask TaskNotFoundError
SubscribeToTask UnsupportedOperationError: Streaming is not supported by the agent
entries.notes: SubscribeToTask against a card whose streaming capability is false or absent answers UnsupportedOperationError (-32004) over JSON-RPC (test added 2026-10-10, shown to fail with the check disabled). No-op when no card is configured; see §8.1 line 1980.

entries.requirement: SubscribeToTask TaskNotFoundError
UnsupportedOperationError: The operation is attempted on a task that is in a terminal state
The stream MUST terminate when the task reaches a terminal state
entries.notes: SubscribeToTask streams through the same reader, so it now ends at the terminal event (2026-10-12), and stays open across turns until one (STREAM-SUB-002). Remaining, by design and pinned by a test: after subscribe_max_idle (default 300 s) with the task still non-terminal the reattach hook ends the stream early; the client resubscribes.

entries.requirement: The operation MUST return a `Task` object as the first event in the stream, representing the current state of the task at the time of subscription.
PushNotificationNotSupportedError (create)
TaskNotFoundError (create)
The operation MUST establish a webhook endpoint for task update notifications.
The configuration MUST persist until task completion or explicit deletion.
entries.notes: No eviction/TTL in any push-config store; retention only purges terminal tasks. InMemoryPushConfigStore loses configs on process restart (inherent to in-memory).

entries.requirement: PushNotificationNotSupportedError (get)
entries.notes: Card-only: with no card and no push sender, Get/List/Delete still run against the store (only Create checks push_sender).

entries.requirement: TaskNotFoundError: The push notification configuration does not exist.
The operation MUST return configuration details including webhook URL and notification settings.
entries.notes: Test asserts URL only; whole stored config is returned.

entries.requirement: The operation MUST fail if the configuration does not exist or the client lacks access.
entries.notes: With RequestHandlerBuilder::isolate_tasks_by_caller the authenticated caller's identity selects the store partition (TenantContext::partition), so another caller's task is TaskNotFound like an unknown id and lists hold only the caller's own; the SDK enforces it, the agent author turns it on (off by default: sharing within a tenant stays the default). Shared-access models (roles, groups) map the group to a tenant with a TenantResolver. Before this branch: Non-existence is enforced and tested; 'lacks access' is only tenant-granular (needs a TenantResolver + tenant-aware push store) and otherwise left to an interceptor; any caller in the same tenant can read any config by (taskId, id).

entries.requirement: PushNotificationNotSupportedError (list)
TaskNotFoundError: The task ID does not exist or is not accessible. (ListTaskPushNotificationConfigs)
entries.notes: RequestHandler::require_task checks the task before listing; an unknown task is TaskNotFound (REST 404, JSON-RPC -32001), as in the reference SDK. A test that asserted the old empty list was corrected.

entries.requirement: The operation MUST return all active push notification configurations for the specified task
and MAY support pagination for tasks with many configurations.
entries.notes: pageSize/pageToken are ignored and nextPageToken is always None; the list is bounded by max_push_configs_per_task.

entries.requirement: PushNotificationNotSupportedError (delete)
TaskNotFoundError: The task ID does not exist. (DeleteTaskPushNotificationConfig)
entries.notes: The task must exist (TaskNotFound otherwise); deleting a config that is already gone on an existing task still succeeds, keeping the operation idempotent.

entries.requirement: The operation MUST permanently remove the specified push notification configuration.
entries.notes: Delivery re-lists configs per event (push_delivery/mod.rs:72), so later events are not sent to a deleted webhook; no test asserts 'no notification after delete'.

entries.requirement: This operation MUST be idempotent - multiple deletions of the same config have the same effect.
UnsupportedOperationError: The agent does not support authenticated extended cards
ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError: The agent declares support but does not have an extended agent card configured.
entries.notes: Returned only when no card at all is configured; since the extended card IS the public card (see line 424), 'declares support but not configured' cannot otherwise occur.

entries.requirement: The client MUST authenticate the request using one of the schemes declared in the public AgentCard.securitySchemes and AgentCard.security fields.
entries.notes: Client: get_extended_agent_card does not check that credentials matching the card's schemes are attached; the caller must register AuthInterceptor. Server side refuses the call unless an authenticating interceptor exists (or allow_unauthenticated_extended_card opt-out).

entries.requirement: The operation MAY return different details based on client authentication level, including additional skills, capabilities, or configuration not available in the public Agent Card.
entries.notes: extended_card_for_this_call returns `card.clone()` of the same `self.agent_card` that backs /.well-known/agent-card.json; the builder has no separate extended-card setting, so the 'extended' card is always identical to the public one.

entries.requirement: Clients retrieving this extended card SHOULD replace their cached public Agent Card with the content received from this endpoint for the duration of their authenticated session or until the card's version changes.
entries.notes: The client just returns the card; A2aClient keeps no card, and CachingCardResolver exposes only resolve()/invalidate(), so there is no SDK hook to install the extended card into the cache. The caller must do this itself.

entries.requirement: Blocking (`return_immediately: false` or unset): The operation MUST wait until the task reaches a terminal state ... or an interrupted state ... before returning.
entries.notes: collect_events loops until `is_terminal() || is_interrupted()` (sync_collector.rs:242). Edge: if the executor returns without ever reaching a terminal/interrupted state, the collector drains (bounded by executor_drain_timeout) and answers with the non-terminal state (sync_collector.rs:205-221) -- an agent bug, but the SDK does not force a terminal state there.

entries.requirement: The response MUST include the latest task state with all artifacts and status information.
entries.notes: Artifacts are folded into the collected task and returned. Note the response omits `history` unless historyLength is set (respond.rs:36-48, decisions.rs:34), which the spec's 'implementation-defined default' for unset historyLength permits.

entries.requirement: Non-Blocking (`return_immediately: true`): The operation MUST return immediately after creating the task, even if processing is still in progress.
entries.notes: Returns the Submitted snapshot and spawns the background processor; test asserts state==Submitted and that the store later reaches Completed.

entries.requirement: historyLength 0: No history should be returned; the `history` field SHOULD be omitted
entries.notes: truncate_history returns None for n==0, so the field is omitted (not []) on GetTask, ListTasks and SendMessage responses.

entries.requirement: Custom protocol bindings MUST specify how service parameters are transmitted in their binding specification.
entries.notes: WebSocket: the binding specification (book/src/bindings/websocket.md §2) states the mechanism (upgrade headers, once per connection), the A2A-Version query fallback, value constraints, the reserved :path key, and that parameters cannot vary per request. SLIMRPC: slimrpc.md §3. The page's wire claims are pinned by websocket_binding_spec.rs (handshake refusal and query fallback, refusal codes and ErrorInfo, stream frames and marker), which passed against the page as written.

entries.requirement: A2A-Extensions: Comma-separated list of extension URIs that the client wants to use for the request (implied: server reads it as a service parameter; client can send it)
entries.notes: Server parses the lowercased `a2a-extensions` header/metadata on all bindings via build_call_context. Client has no first-class API to declare extensions; callers must add the header through extra headers/interceptors (no A2A_EXTENSIONS_HEADER use in crates/a2a-protocol-client/src outside a retry.rs comment).

entries.requirement: A2A-Version: ... If the version is not supported, the agent returns VersionNotSupportedError
entries.notes: Every binding, the axum adapter included (validate_a2a_request middleware), answers VersionNotSupportedError.

entries.requirement: As service parameter names MAY need to co-exist with other parameters ... all service parameters defined by this specification will be prefixed with `a2a-`.
entries.notes: Naming rule for the spec itself; SDK constants use the `A2A-` prefix.

entries.requirement: Send Message operations MAY be idempotent. Agents may utilize the messageId to detect duplicate messages.
entries.notes: Implemented through an opt-in idempotency extension key in message metadata (IDEMPOTENCY_EXTENSION_URI), not by messageId alone.

entries.requirement: A duplicate cancellation request MAY return `TaskNotFoundError` if the task has already been canceled and purged.
entries.notes: Purged task -> TaskNotFound (store miss). A duplicate cancel of a still-stored Canceled task returns TaskNotCancelableError (cancel_task.rs:48), consistent with that error's definition though not literally 'the same effect' as the first cancel.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST return appropriate errors
entries.notes: Every ServerError maps to an ErrorCode, HTTP status and gRPC code; covered by per-code unit tests.

entries.requirement: Servers ... SHOULD provide actionable information to help clients resolve issues.
entries.notes: Refusals name the parameter and the accepted form or limit; the wire test pins six (message.id empty and too long, no parts, metadata over the size limit and not an object, unsupported A2A-Version). Shown to fail with the message.id label changed.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST reject requests with invalid or missing authentication credentials
entries.notes: SDK provides ApiKey/Bearer/JWT interceptors mapped to 401/UNAUTHENTICATED on all bindings, but nothing auto-enforces a card's securityRequirements: without an interceptor every operation except GetExtendedAgentCard (extended_card.rs:79) is served unauthenticated.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD include authentication challenge information in the error response
entries.notes: WWW-Authenticate added on HTTP bindings for 401; WebSocket answers per-message after upgrade with body only (auth/mod.rs doc), so no challenge there.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD specify which authentication scheme is required
entries.notes: Challenge carries the scheme (e.g. `Bearer realm="a2a"`).

entries.requirement: Servers MUST return an authorization error when the authenticated client lacks required permissions
entries.notes: Hook: an interceptor returns A2aError::permission_denied -> 403 / PERMISSION_DENIED. Permission policy itself is the application's.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD indicate what permission or scope is missing (without leaking sensitive information ...)
entries.notes: permission_denied takes a caller-chosen message; SDK has no structured scope field.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST NOT reveal the existence of resources the client is not authorized to access
entries.notes: With RequestHandlerBuilder::isolate_tasks_by_caller the authenticated caller's identity selects the store partition (TenantContext::partition), so another caller's task is TaskNotFound like an unknown id and lists hold only the caller's own; the SDK enforces it, the agent author turns it on (off by default: sharing within a tenant stays the default). Shared-access models (roles, groups) map the group to a tenant with a TenantResolver. Before this branch: Cross-tenant lookups miss and return TaskNotFound (indistinguishable). Within one tenant there is no per-principal ownership: any caller passing the interceptors can Get/Cancel/Subscribe any task id; per-user scoping (spec's 'task created by another user' example) requires a custom TaskStore/tenant resolver.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST validate all input parameters before processing
entries.notes: validate_send_params runs before any side effect (ids, parts, input modes, metadata shape/size).

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD specify which parameter(s) failed validation and why
entries.notes: Each handler validation message names the parameter (message.id, message, request metadata, A2A version); body-shape errors also carry a google.rpc.BadRequest field violation (jsonrpc_error_details.rs). The handler's own validation errors name the field in text only, not as a BadRequest detail: ServerError::InvalidParams carries a String, and changing it would break callers that match it.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD provide guidance on valid parameter values or formats
entries.notes: Messages state the limit or accepted value ("got 5000, max ...", "max 1048576", "must be a JSON object", "this server supports 1.x"); pinned by the wire test.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST return a not found error when a requested resource does not exist or is not accessible to the authenticated client
entries.notes: TaskNotFound (404/NOT_FOUND/-32001) for missing tasks and push configs on every binding.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD NOT distinguish between "does not exist" and "not authorized"
entries.notes: Tenant-scoped store returns None for another tenant's task, which surfaces as the same TaskNotFound.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD return appropriate error codes for temporary failures vs. permanent errors
entries.notes: Overloaded -> 503 with an AIP-193 status of RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED); Halted -> 503 / UNAVAILABLE; a rate-limit refusal -> 429 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; internal -> 500 / INTERNAL. Until 2026-10-10 an overload's REST body read status INTERNAL under 503, naming a permanent failure.

entries.requirement: Servers MAY include retry guidance (e.g., Retry-After header in HTTP)
entries.notes: A rate-limit refusal carries Retry-After (whole seconds to the end of the window) on HTTP+JSON and a RetryInfo detail on every binding. Overload (503) and halt (503) send no retry guidance: neither has a known end.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD log system errors for diagnostic purposes
entries.notes: Failures are recorded on the RPC span (error.type, otel.status_code=ERROR) and in metrics.on_error; trace_error! for executor panics. Behind the `tracing` feature; no test asserts that an Internal error is logged.

entries.requirement: All error responses ... MUST convey ... Error Code ... Error Message
entries.notes: JSON-RPC {code,message,data}, REST AIP-193 {code,status,message,details}, gRPC Status(code,message,details).

entries.requirement: Each object in the [details] array MUST include a `@type` key
entries.notes: Only ErrorInfo with '@type: type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo' is emitted; executor-supplied A2aError.data is dropped by the dispatchers (they rebuild details from error_info_data), so no untyped detail can reach the wire.

entries.requirement: Well-known types from the google.rpc error model (e.g., ErrorInfo, BadRequest) SHOULD be used where applicable
entries.notes: ErrorInfo on every A2A-specific error. Since ef31df9 a body or params that do not deserialize carry google.rpc.BadRequest with the field path (jsonrpc_error_details.rs, bad_request_details.rs). Remaining: the handler's own validation failures (empty message.id, no parts, oversize metadata) name the field in the message only, because ServerError::InvalidParams carries a String.

entries.requirement: Protocol bindings MUST map these elements to their native error representations while preserving semantic meaning
entries.notes: Per-code mappings to HTTP status and gRPC code are unit tested.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY accept additional messages for tasks in non-terminal states to enable multi-turn interactions
entries.notes: Non-terminal continuations reuse the task id; a send to a task whose executor is still running is refused (UnsupportedOperation), see tests.rs concurrent_send_to_in_flight_task_is_rejected.

entries.requirement: When clients attempt to use operations or features that require capabilities not declared ... the agent MUST return an appropriate error response
entries.notes: Summary of 573-576 below. All checks are skipped when no AgentCard is configured on the RequestHandler (capability.rs:16-18, 189).

entries.requirement: If AgentCard.capabilities.pushNotifications is false or not present, push notification config operations (Create, Get, List, Delete) MUST return PushNotificationNotSupportedError
entries.notes: All four ops checked; also PushNotSupported when no push sender is wired.

entries.requirement: If AgentCard.capabilities.streaming is false or not present, SendStreamingMessage or SubscribeToTask MUST return UnsupportedOperationError
entries.notes: ensure_streaming_supported refuses SendStreamingMessage and SubscribeToTask unless capabilities.streaming is true. Tested over JSON-RPC for streaming false and absent (code -32004 on both methods, against an existing task); shown to fail with the check disabled. A no-op when no card is configured.

entries.requirement: If AgentCard.capabilities.extendedAgentCard is false or not present, Get Extended Agent Card MUST return UnsupportedOperationError. If the agent declares support but has not configured an extended card, it MUST return ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError.
entries.notes: There is no separate extended-card slot: the handler's own agent_card is returned as the extended card, so NotConfigured is only produced when the handler has no card at all.

entries.requirement: When a server requests use of an extension marked as `required: true` ... but the client does not declare support for it, the agent MUST return ExtensionSupportRequiredError
entries.notes: Every operation now refuses a client that does not declare a required extension; GetExtendedAgentCard was the one that skipped it.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD validate capability support by examining the Agent Card before attempting operations that require optional capabilities
entries.notes: Client reads card.capabilities only for the idempotency extension (builder/mod.rs:203); stream/subscribe/push-config calls are sent regardless of capabilities.streaming/pushNotifications (no such check in crates/a2a-protocol-client/src).

entries.requirement: Agents MAY generate a new contextId when processing a Message that does not include a contextId field
entries.notes: UUIDv4 generated.

entries.requirement: If an agent generates a new contextId, it MUST be included in the response (either Task or Message)
entries.notes: Task responses always carry context_id. A direct Message reply whose contextId the executor left empty now gets the task's contextId, on the blocking path and on a message-only stream; a contextId the executor set is kept. Until 2026-10-10 such a reply named no context.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY accept and preserve client-provided contextId values
entries.notes: Client contextId used verbatim after validation.

entries.requirement: If an agent cannot accept a client-provided contextId, it MUST reject the request with an error and MUST NOT generate a new contextId for the response
entries.notes: Invalid contextId -> InvalidParams before any task is created; a provided contextId is never replaced.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD NOT provide a client-generated contextId to a server unless they understand how the server will process that contextId
entries.notes: The client SDK never fills context_id itself; the caller builds the Message.

entries.requirement: Server-generated contextId values SHOULD be treated as opaque identifiers by clients
entries.notes: ContextId is an opaque string newtype; the client SDK never parses it.

entries.requirement: All tasks and messages with the same contextId SHOULD be treated as part of the same conversational session
entries.notes: SDK groups by context (find_task_by_context, per-context lock) and passes context_id to the executor; conversational semantics are the agent's.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY use the contextId to maintain internal state, conversational history, or LLM context
entries.notes: context_id exposed on RequestContext.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY implement context expiration or cleanup policies
entries.notes: Task-store TTL/capacity and retention modules.

entries.requirement: [Agents] SHOULD document any such policies
entries.notes: Deployment-specific; SDK documents its own TTL/capacity knobs in rustdoc.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST generate a unique taskId for each new task they create
entries.notes: UUIDv4 per new task; test asserts a new id on a new round in the same context.

entries.requirement: The generated taskId MUST be included in the Task object returned to the client
entries.notes: Task.id is a required field; tests read task.id from the response and fetch it from the store.

entries.requirement: When a client includes a taskId in a Message, it MUST reference an existing task
entries.notes: Client-side obligation; the server enforces it (line 614).

entries.requirement: Agents MUST return a TaskNotFoundError if the provided taskId does not correspond to an existing task
Clients MAY include the contextId in subsequent messages
entries.notes: Message.context_id field exposed.

entries.requirement: Clients MAY use taskId (with or without contextId) to continue or refine a specific task
Clients MAY use contextId without taskId to start a new task within an existing conversation context
Agents MUST infer contextId from the task if only taskId is provided
Agents MUST reject messages containing mismatching contextId and taskId
entries.notes: Rejected with InvalidParams.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD use the referenceTaskIds field in Message to explicitly reference related tasks
entries.notes: Field exposed on Message; client SDK never sets it.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD use referenced tasks to understand the context and intent of follow-up requests
entries.notes: Executor receives message.reference_task_ids raw; unlike some SDKs the referenced Tasks are not resolved/loaded into RequestContext (fields at request_context.rs:40-70), so the agent must hold its own store handle to look them up.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD leverage the shared contextId to provide contextually relevant responses
All implementations MUST deliver events in the order they were generated. Events MUST NOT be reordered during transmission
entries.notes: Single tokio broadcast channel per task; SSE/gRPC/WS writers forward sequentially.

entries.requirement: An agent MAY serve multiple concurrent streams to one or more clients for the same task
Events MUST be broadcast to all active streams for that task
Each stream MUST receive the same events in the same order
entries.notes: Order is preserved, but a subscriber that falls behind the bounded broadcast buffer loses the overwritten events (surfaced as an explicit 'streamLagged' error), so a slow stream does not receive the same events as a fast one.

entries.requirement: Closing one stream MUST NOT affect other active streams for the same task
entries.notes: Readers are independent broadcast::Receivers and nothing cancels a task when a stream closes. The test drops the originating SendStreamingMessage stream and checks a SubscribeToTask stream still reaches the terminal event. Not injection-proven: no single-point code fault produces the violation today; the test guards against adding one (e.g. cancel-on-disconnect).

entries.requirement: Patch version numbers SHOULD NOT be used in requests, responses and Agent Cards
entries.notes: A2A_VERSION = "1.0" used for headers and card builder; some test fixtures use "1.0.0" but no production path does.

entries.requirement: [Patch version numbers] MUST not be considered when clients and servers negotiate protocol versions
entries.notes: Only the major is compared on both sides.

entries.requirement: Clients MUST send the A2A-Version header with each request
entries.notes: All four transports set it; JSON-RPC/REST covered implicitly by e2e tests against the default (version-required) RestDispatcher/JsonRpcDispatcher. WebSocket sends it on the upgrade only (per connection).

entries.requirement: Clients MAY provide the A2A-Version as a request parameter instead of a header.
entries.notes: Client always uses the header (fine).

entries.requirement: (implied) Server must honour A2A-Version supplied as a request parameter (`?A2A-Version=1.0`), since clients MAY send it that way and agents MUST process the requested version
entries.notes: dispatch::requested_version reads the header, else the ?A2A-Version= parameter, on JSON-RPC, REST, the WebSocket upgrade and axum.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST process requests using the semantics of the requested A2A-Version (matching Major.Minor).
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-12 (maintainer decision) a request is served only when its A2A-Version names this server's Major.Minor, 1.0, with any patch; any other version, 1.1 included, is VersionNotSupportedError naming 1.0, on every binding through one validator (the WebSocket handshake had its own copy). Until then any 1.x was accepted and served with 1.0 semantics, as the official Python SDK still does (_is_version_compatible compares the major only).

entries.requirement: If the version is not supported by the interface, agents MUST return a VersionNotSupportedError.
entries.notes: The axum adapter now validates A2A-Version like the other bindings.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST interpret empty value as 0.3 version.
entries.notes: Empty means 0.3 and is refused on every binding including axum. Only the explicit opt-outs (accept_missing_version_header, gRPC require_version_header=false) serve it as 1.0, by the deployer's choice.

entries.requirement: Tooling libraries and SDKs ... MUST provide mechanisms to help clients manage protocol versioning, such as negotiation of the transport and protocol version used.
entries.notes: ClientBuilder::from_card filters interfaces by protocol major then binding preference; server exposes validate_version_metadata for out-of-tree bindings.

entries.requirement: Messages SHOULD NOT be used to deliver task outputs.
entries.notes: Agent's choice; SDK provides TaskUpdater-style artifact() helper.

entries.requirement: Results SHOULD BE returned using Artifacts associated with a Task.
Clients using streaming ... MAY not receive all status update messages if the client is disconnected and then reconnects.
entries.notes: Informative allowance; SDK additionally offers SSE resumption (sse_resumption_e2e.rs) which narrows the gap.

entries.requirement: Messages MUST NOT be considered a reliable delivery mechanism for critical information.
entries.notes: Design guidance for agent/client authors; not testable in the SDK.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY choose to persist all Messages that contain important information in the Task history
entries.notes: SDK persists every agent Message event into Task.history (capped at 1024).

entries.requirement: clients MUST NOT rely on this behavior unless negotiated out-of-band.
entries.notes: Client-author obligation.

entries.requirement: All protocol bindings MUST provide functionally equivalent representations of these data structures.
entries.notes: One domain model (serde JSON) with a prost conversion layer for gRPC; golden fixtures from the official Python SDK prove JSON<->proto equivalence.

entries.requirement: The agent MUST include authentication credentials in the request headers as specified in the TaskPushNotificationConfig.authentication field.
entries.notes: The sender writes Authorization for Bearer and Basic (case-insensitive), as a2a-go v2.5.0 does. A config naming any other scheme is now refused at creation with InvalidParams, so no webhook is called without the credentials its config specifies. Until 2026-10-10 such a config was stored and delivered without credentials (a2a-go still does that). The sender's runtime drop remains for configs stored before.

entries.requirement: Clients MUST respond with HTTP 2xx status codes to acknowledge successful receipt
entries.notes: Binds the webhook receiver (client-side app). SDK ships no webhook receiver; only `push::webhook::notification_token` header helper. Sender side treats any 2xx as success (sender.rs:925).

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD process notifications idempotently, as duplicate deliveries may occur
entries.notes: Webhook receiver concern; no SDK receiver/dedup hook provided.

entries.requirement: Clients MUST validate the task ID matches an expected task
entries.notes: Webhook receiver concern; SDK provides no receiver or task-id validation helper (only token header extraction).

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD implement appropriate security measures to verify the notification source
entries.notes: SDK hook: sender emits the config token under both X-A2A-Notification-Token and A2A-Notification-Token; receiver can read it with webhook::notification_token. Verification itself is the app's.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST attempt delivery at least once for each configured webhook
entries.notes: Every configured webhook is attempted for every event, on the background and blocking paths. push_delivery_budget now sets concurrency: ceil(configs / (budget / timeout)), at least 1, at most configs (17 at the defaults); events go in order per webhook. Until 2026-10-11 deliveries were sequential and the budget skipped the rest (6 of 100 reached at defaults). PushRetryPolicy max_attempts 0 is taken as 1 (setter and loop). Not covered: a webhook whose single attempt exceeds push_delivery_timeout is cut off, which is an attempt, not a skip.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY implement retry logic with exponential backoff for failed deliveries
entries.notes: PushRetryPolicy default 3 attempts, backoff [1s,2s]; only 5xx/408/429/transport errors are retried.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD include a reasonable timeout for webhook requests (recommended: 10-30 seconds)
entries.notes: Timeouts exist: per-request 30s in HttpPushSender, but the handler wraps each send in `push_delivery_timeout` = 5s default, below the recommended 10-30s and (as the code's own comment notes) truncating the sender's retry schedule to one attempt.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY stop attempting delivery after a configured number of consecutive failures
entries.notes: max_attempts per delivery; non-retryable 4xx stops immediately.

entries.requirement: Extensions SHOULD include version information in their URI identifier.
entries.notes: Extension authors choose URIs; SDK treats URIs as opaque strings.

entries.requirement: A new URI MUST be created for breaking changes to an extension.
entries.notes: Process requirement on extension authors; not code-testable.

entries.requirement: If a client requests a version of an extension that the agent does not support, the agent SHOULD ignore the extension for that interaction and proceed without it
entries.notes: Activated set is the exact-string intersection of A2A-Extensions request header and card-declared URIs; undeclared URIs are silently ignored and not echoed.

entries.requirement: unless the extension is marked as required in the AgentCard, in which case the agent MUST return an error indicating unsupported extension
entries.notes: Handler-level check (all bindings; gRPC metadata is converted to the same header map) returns ExtensionSupportRequiredError (-32008) naming missing URIs. Note: GetExtendedAgentCard does not call ensure_required_extensions (extended_card.rs has no call).

entries.requirement: It MUST NOT fall back to a previous version of the extension automatically.
entries.notes: Extension URIs match by exact string equality: a client declaring .../v2 neither satisfies a required .../v1 nor activates an optional one. Shown to fail with version-agnostic matching injected.

entries.requirement: Identical Functionality: Provide the same set of operations and capabilities
entries.notes: All 11 operations are routed on JSON-RPC, REST, gRPC and WebSocket (TCK --equivalence). WebSocket's leftover v0.3 alias message/stream was removed on 2026-10-12 and is now -32601 as over HTTP; shown to fail with the alias restored.

entries.requirement: Consistent Behavior: Return semantically equivalent results for the same requests
entries.notes: All bindings dispatch to the same RequestHandler; TCK compares task views across the four bindings in CI.

entries.requirement: Same Error Handling: Map errors consistently using appropriate protocol-specific codes
entries.notes: Single ErrorCode table drives HTTP status, gRPC code and JSON-RPC code.

entries.requirement: Equivalent Authentication: Support the same authentication schemes declared in the AgentCard
entries.notes: Auth is enforced by handler-level interceptors common to all bindings; CI runs a secured SUT and checks rejection+acceptance on all four bindings (tck.yml:217).

entries.requirement: Agents MUST declare all supported protocols in their AgentCard
entries.notes: Card content is author-supplied; builder only rejects an empty supported_interfaces, it does not cross-check against the dispatchers actually served.

entries.requirement: Clients MAY choose any protocol declared by the agent
entries.notes: from_card_preferring / with_protocol_binding.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD implement fallback logic for alternative protocols
entries.notes: Fallback is build-time only (next interface when the chosen one cannot be constructed); there is no runtime fallback on connection failure.

entries.requirement: All A2A-specific errors defined in Section 3.3.2 MUST be mapped to binding-specific error representations.
entries.notes: ErrorCode enum is the single source; http_status()/grpc_status() derive per-binding codes; gRPC adds google.rpc.ErrorInfo.

entries.requirement: (table) TaskNotFoundError -> JSON-RPC -32001, gRPC NOT_FOUND, HTTP 404
entries.notes: Matches the v1.0.1 table (identical to main). Unit-level assertions on the table functions; gRPC dispatcher derives tonic::Code from grpc_status().

entries.requirement: (table) TaskNotCancelableError -> JSON-RPC -32002, gRPC FAILED_PRECONDITION, HTTP 400
entries.notes: Matches the v1.0.1 table (identical to main). Unit-level assertions on the table functions; gRPC dispatcher derives tonic::Code from grpc_status().

entries.requirement: (table) PushNotificationNotSupportedError -> JSON-RPC -32003, gRPC FAILED_PRECONDITION, HTTP 400
entries.notes: Matches the v1.0.1 table (identical to main). Unit-level assertions on the table functions; gRPC dispatcher derives tonic::Code from grpc_status().

entries.requirement: (table) UnsupportedOperationError -> JSON-RPC -32004, gRPC FAILED_PRECONDITION, HTTP 400
entries.notes: Matches the v1.0.1 table (identical to main). Unit-level assertions on the table functions; gRPC dispatcher derives tonic::Code from grpc_status().

entries.requirement: (table) ContentTypeNotSupportedError -> JSON-RPC -32005, gRPC INVALID_ARGUMENT, HTTP 400
entries.notes: Matches the v1.0.1 table (identical to main). Unit-level assertions on the table functions; gRPC dispatcher derives tonic::Code from grpc_status().

entries.requirement: (table) InvalidAgentResponseError -> JSON-RPC -32006, gRPC INTERNAL, HTTP 500
entries.notes: Matches the v1.0.1 table (identical to main). Unit-level assertions on the table functions; gRPC dispatcher derives tonic::Code from grpc_status().

entries.requirement: (table) ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError -> JSON-RPC -32007, gRPC FAILED_PRECONDITION, HTTP 400
entries.notes: Matches the v1.0.1 table (identical to main). Unit-level assertions on the table functions; gRPC dispatcher derives tonic::Code from grpc_status().

entries.requirement: (table) ExtensionSupportRequiredError -> JSON-RPC -32008, gRPC FAILED_PRECONDITION, HTTP 400
entries.notes: Matches the v1.0.1 table (identical to main). Unit-level assertions on the table functions; gRPC dispatcher derives tonic::Code from grpc_status().

entries.requirement: (table) VersionNotSupportedError -> JSON-RPC -32009, gRPC FAILED_PRECONDITION, HTTP 400
entries.notes: Matches the v1.0.1 table (identical to main). Unit-level assertions on the table functions; gRPC dispatcher derives tonic::Code from grpc_status().

entries.requirement: Custom protocol bindings MUST define equivalent error code mappings that preserve the semantic meaning of each A2A error type.
entries.notes: WebSocket reuses the JSON-RPC codes verbatim, documented in its binding spec §5. Remaining: SLIMRPC's RpcCode mapping for PushNotSupported/UnsupportedOperation/VersionNotSupported (UNIMPLEMENTED) differs from A2A §5.4's gRPC column (FAILED_PRECONDITION); this is the SLIMRPC spec's own mapping (2985, maintainer/upstream).

entries.requirement: The binding specification SHOULD provide a similar mapping table showing how each A2A error type is represented in the custom binding's native error format.
entries.notes: WebSocket now has an error mapping table (binding spec §5). Remaining: SLIMRPC's vendored upstream table omits -32007/-32008/-32009.

entries.requirement: All JSON serializations of the A2A protocol data model MUST use camelCase naming for field names
entries.notes: All Serialize structs carry rename_all=camelCase (scripted scan found none with snake_case fields lacking it); snake_case accepted as input alias only (proto_field_alias.rs).

entries.requirement: Enum values MUST be represented according to the ProtoJSON specification ... (typically SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE).
entries.notes: TaskState/Role (the only proto enums) serialize as TASK_STATE_*/ROLE_*; legacy lowercase accepted as aliases on input.

entries.requirement: Protocol Buffer enum: TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED -> JSON value: "TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED"
entries.notes: Keyword appears only inside an enum identifier in an example; covered by the §5.5 enum entry.

entries.requirement: When serialized to JSON ... timestamps MUST be represented as ISO 8601 formatted strings in UTC timezone.
entries.notes: Every executor event passes the queue writer, which stamps an empty status timestamp with UTC now, rewrites one with a non-Z offset to the same instant in UTC (millisecond precision), and refuses one that does not parse as ISO 8601. Until 2026-10-10 an executor-set value went out unchanged on JSON-RPC/REST/WebSocket. Not covered: a Task an application writes straight to the task store, bypassing the queue.

entries.requirement: Millisecond precision SHOULD be used where available
entries.notes: utc_now_iso8601 formats YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ.

entries.requirement: Clients and servers MUST parse and generate ISO 8601 timestamps correctly
entries.notes: Server rejects malformed statusTimestampAfter with InvalidParams; JSON-path clients keep timestamps as opaque strings (no parsing needed).

entries.requirement: When millisecond precision is not available, the fractional seconds portion MAY be omitted or zero-filled
entries.notes: Parser accepts with and without fractional seconds.

entries.requirement: Timestamps MUST NOT include timezone offsets other than 'Z' (all times are UTC)
entries.notes: Every executor event passes the queue writer, which stamps an empty status timestamp with UTC now, rewrites one with a non-Z offset to the same instant in UTC (millisecond precision), and refuses one that does not parse as ISO 8601. Until 2026-10-10 an executor-set value went out unchanged on JSON-RPC/REST/WebSocket. Not covered: a Task an application writes straight to the task store, bypassing the queue.

entries.requirement: ...annotations to indicate whether fields are REQUIRED. These annotations serve as both documentation and validation hints
entries.notes: Descriptive; requirements are in the next entries.

entries.requirement: Fields marked REQUIRED indicate that the field MUST be present and set in valid messages.
entries.notes: Non-Option serde fields make absence a parse error (InvalidParams); ids validated non-empty/bounded by validate_id.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD validate these requirements and reject messages with missing required fields.
entries.notes: Inbound requests validated by typed deserialization plus explicit checks.

entries.requirement: Arrays marked as required MUST contain at least one element.
entries.notes: Enforced for Message.parts and Artifact.parts (before), and since 2026-10-11 for the published AgentCard: validate refuses empty defaultInputModes, defaultOutputModes, skills, or a skill's tags; build() runs it, the dynamic handler answers 500 for an invalid produced card, hot reload refuses one. Remaining, why PARTIAL/low: (1) ListTasksResponse.tasks is REQUIRED-repeated in the proto yet legitimately empty for a listing with no matches, a contradiction inside the specification; the SDK returns the empty list. (2) HotReloadAgentCardHandler::new and update are infallible and do not validate (a change would break their signatures). Client-side parsing stays tolerant on purpose.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD ignore unrecognized fields in messages
entries.notes: No deny_unknown_fields anywhere in types/server/client src.

entries.requirement: Custom protocol bindings SHOULD be identified by a URI.
entries.notes: WebSocket: https://a2a-rust.com/bindings/websocket/v1; SlimRPC: https://a2a-protocol.org/bindings/experimental-slimrpc/v1.

entries.requirement: The protocolBinding field in the Agent Card's supportedInterfaces entry SHOULD be a URI
entries.notes: SDK provides WEBSOCKET_BINDING_URI constant for card authors; card content is author-supplied.

entries.requirement: When a breaking change is introduced to a binding, a new URI MUST be used
entries.notes: Process requirement; both custom-binding URIs carry /v1, no breaking revision exists yet.

entries.requirement: UTF-8 encoding MUST be used for JSON text
entries.notes: serde_json emits UTF-8 and rejects invalid UTF-8. A body with a Latin-1 byte answers -32700 on JSON-RPC and 400 on HTTP+JSON; shown to fail with lossy decoding injected.

entries.requirement: Content MUST be validated against the A2A protocol schema before processing
entries.notes: Typed deserialization plus handler validation before executor invocation.

entries.requirement: Implementations MUST sanitize user-provided content to prevent injection attacks
entries.notes: SDK guards header injection in push creds (validate_header_value) and path traversal in REST; sanitising message content for downstream use is the executor's job.

entries.requirement: File references within A2A messages MUST be validated to prevent SSRF
entries.notes: SDK never dereferences Part URLs; SSRF validation exists only for push webhooks and is pub(crate), so no reusable hook is exposed to executors for file URIs.

entries.requirement: Authentication and authorization MUST be enforced as specified in Section 7
entries.notes: SDK provides auth interceptors (Bearer/JWT); operator must register them. Detailed §7 audit is outside this range.

entries.requirement: Sensitive information in task history and artifacts MUST be protected according to applicable data protection regulations
entries.notes: Deployment/regulatory obligation.

entries.requirement: The A2A-Version value MUST be in the format Major.Minor
entries.notes: Client sends "1.0" on all transports; server rejects non-1.x with VersionNotSupportedError (accepts any 1.x incl. patch).

entries.requirement: The resource at this URI MUST return an AgentCard object
entries.notes: 404 when no card configured.

entries.requirement: The Agent Card MAY contain public information about an agent's capabilities
[Agent Card] SHOULD NOT include sensitive credentials or internal implementation details
entries.notes: Card content is author-supplied; no SDK lint.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD support HTTPS to ensure authenticity and integrity of the Agent Card
entries.notes: Client fetches over HTTPS (rustls). Server HTTP listeners (serve/, JSON-RPC/REST/WS) do not terminate TLS; docs require a reverse proxy; only gRPC has native TLS (grpc-tls).

entries.requirement: Agent Cards MAY be signed using JWS
entries.notes: Signing/verification in a2a-protocol-types::signing.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD verify signatures when present
entries.notes: With CardFetchOptions::with_signature_keys (feature signing), resolve_agent_card_with_options and fetch_card_from_url_with_options return a signed card only if one signature verifies against the caller's keys; a tampered card or one with no matching key fails the fetch; an unsigned card is returned. Why PARTIAL/low: verification needs keys only the application can trust, so it is opt-in, not default; CachingCardResolver and ClientBuilder::from_card do not take keys yet; jku is never followed (the card cannot vouch for its own keys, §8.4.3 line 2132).

entries.requirement: Extended Agent Cards ... MAY contain additional information
entries.notes: Note: handler returns the same configured agent_card; no separate extended-card content in this handler.

entries.requirement: [Extended Agent Cards] MUST enforce appropriate access controls
entries.notes: Refuses unless an authenticating interceptor is registered or operator opts out explicitly.

entries.requirement: All legacy names and anchors MUST remain resolvable until the stated earliest removal version.
entries.notes: Spec-document anchor requirement.

entries.requirement: Each legacy span SHOULD be placed adjacent to the current object's heading
entries.notes: Spec-document editorial requirement.

entries.requirement: Client Implementations SHOULD: prefer new names; implement dual-handling; log a warning when receiving legacy-named objects
entries.notes: New names emitted; dual-handling for legacy enum spellings and AgentCard.url (parse-only). No fallback for legacy `supportsExtendedAgentCard` (no occurrence in code) and no warning is logged on legacy forms.

entries.requirement: Server Implementations MAY accept both legacy and current request message forms; emit only current form
entries.notes: Aliases accept legacy input; skip_serializing keeps output current-form.

entries.requirement: Until then, edits MUST be manual and reviewed in PRs affecting a2a.proto.
entries.notes: Spec-repo process.

entries.requirement: Production deployments **MUST** use encrypted communication (HTTPS for HTTP-based bindings, TLS for gRPC).
entries.notes: Deployment obligation. gRPC listener can serve TLS via GrpcDispatcher::with_tls (grpc-tls feature); the JSON-RPC/REST/WebSocket serve paths are plaintext hyper only, so HTTPS must come from a terminating proxy or the user's own axum/TLS stack. Client accepts both http:// and https:// endpoints (no production guard).

entries.requirement: Implementations **SHOULD** use modern TLS configurations (TLS 1.3+ recommended) with strong cipher suites.
entries.notes: rustls 0.23.45 implements only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 (its versions.rs defines no other SupportedProtocolVersion), so SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0/1.1 cannot be offered. The client's config negotiates TLS 1.3 with a server that has it and enables only forward-secret AEAD suites (TLS13_* and TLS_ECDHE_*_GCM/CHACHA20_POLY1305); shown to fail with the client limited to TLS 1.2. TLS 1.2 stays enabled for peers without 1.3. The push sender's default config (push/sender.rs) uses the same builder chain; it is read, not handshake-tested.

entries.requirement: A2A Clients **SHOULD** verify the A2A Server's identity by validating its TLS certificate against trusted certificate authorities (CAs) during the TLS handshake.
entries.notes: Default config uses webpki Mozilla roots; extra roots via tls_config_with_extra_roots; no insecure-skip-verify path found.

entries.requirement: **MUST** authenticate every incoming request based on the provided credentials and its declared authentication requirements.
entries.notes: SDK provides ApiKey/Bearer/JWT ServerInterceptors that run before every method on all bindings, but nothing links the card's securitySchemes/securityRequirements to the interceptor chain: grep for security_requirements/security_schemes in server src (non-test) finds nothing, and build() does not warn when a card declares security but no authenticating interceptor (has_authenticator is only consulted for the extended card). WebSocket per-message auth has no test.

entries.requirement: **SHOULD** use appropriate binding-specific error codes for authentication challenges or rejections.
entries.notes: HTTP 401/403, gRPC UNAUTHENTICATED/PERMISSION_DENIED; WebSocket answers in-body only (no status available after upgrade), untested.

entries.requirement: **SHOULD** provide relevant authentication challenge information with error responses.
entries.notes: WWW-Authenticate: `Bearer realm="a2a"` / `ApiKey header="x-api-key"` on HTTP 401s (JSON-RPC, REST, axum).

entries.requirement: Authorization logic is implementation-specific and **MAY** consider: skills, actions, data access policies, OAuth scopes
entries.notes: Custom ServerInterceptor returning A2aError::permission_denied; caller identity on CallContext.

entries.requirement: MUST use a Task to track the operation it is performing
entries.notes: Executor decides; SDK provides task-tracking EventEmitter.

entries.requirement: MUST transition the TaskState to `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED`
entries.notes: State and its transitions are supported; emitting it is the executor's job.

entries.requirement: MUST include a TaskStatus message explaining the required authorization, unless the details of the authorization have been negotiated out-of-band or via an extension
entries.notes: SDK hook exists (TaskStatus.message), but the convenience EventEmitter::status(state) writes `TaskStatus::new(state)` with no message and there is no auth_required(msg) helper or server-side check, so the easy path emits AUTH_REQUIRED without the required explanation.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST arrange to receive credentials via an out-of-band means, unless an in-band mechanism has been negotiated out-of-band or via an extension.
entries.notes: No SDK mechanism; agent-specific.

entries.requirement: If the credential is received out-of-band, the agent SHOULD maintain any active response streams with the client after setting the TaskState to `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED`.
entries.notes: Server stream ends on terminal state or when the executor's queue closes, not on interrupted states, so an executor that keeps running after writing AUTH_REQUIRED keeps the stream open; no test exercises a stream held open across AUTH_REQUIRED.

entries.requirement: The agent MAY immediately continue Task processing after receiving the credential, without a requirement that clients send a follow-up message.
entries.notes: Executor may keep writing events after AUTH_REQUIRED.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD support receiving messages directed to the Task while the Task remains in `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED`.
entries.notes: Test asserts an authenticated continuation to an AUTH_REQUIRED task is accepted and re-runs the executor (runs==2).

entries.requirement: The client SHOULD follow all In-Task Authorization Agent Responsibilities.
entries.notes: Client-that-is-agent behaviour; delegation helper classifies interrupted states.

entries.requirement: a client SHOULD perform one of the following: Subscribe to Task / Register a webhook / Begin polling the Task
entries.notes: All three hooks exist; client EventStream only finishes on a terminal StatusUpdate (is_terminal, event_stream.rs:688), so it keeps reading after AUTH_REQUIRED. No automatic behaviour.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD receive credentials for in-task authorization requests out of band via a secure channel, such as HTTPS.
entries.notes: Not an SDK concern.

entries.requirement: Credentials SHOULD be bound to the agent which originated the request
entries.notes: No SDK support for credential binding in in-band exchange.

entries.requirement: Credentials containing sensitive information SHOULD be only readable by the agent which originated the request, such as by encrypting the credential.
entries.notes: No SDK support.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST NOT treat the `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED` state transition, by itself, as authorization for any particular operation.
entries.notes: Interceptor chain runs before every method irrespective of task state; server-src mentions of AuthRequired (rpc_span/a2a.rs:50, terminal.rs, store/terminal.rs) are labels/parking only. Note SPEC_COMPLIANCE.md:88 wrongly claims `grep AuthRequired crates/a2a-protocol-server/src` returns no lines.

entries.requirement: The meaning and scope of any resulting authorization decision or credential MUST be defined by the agent's implementation, by the credential issuer, or by an A2A extension.
entries.notes: Definitional; agent/issuer/extension.

entries.requirement: A credential or authorization decision obtained while a Task is in `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED` MUST NOT be assumed to authorize subsequent messages on the Task unless that behavior is explicitly defined
entries.notes: SDK re-authenticates every message (unauthenticated continuation refused, runs stays 1); any credential caching in the executor is the application's responsibility.

entries.requirement: A2A Servers **MUST** make an Agent Card available.
entries.notes: JSON-RPC, REST and axum serve GET /.well-known/agent-card.json when a card is configured, but RequestHandlerBuilder's agent_card defaults to None and build() accepts that, serving 404 (pinned by a test); the WebSocket and gRPC dispatchers serve no well-known card at all, so a WS-only or gRPC-only deployment has no discovery endpoint from the SDK.

entries.requirement: The AgentCard **MUST** properly declare supported protocols
entries.notes: Builder only rejects an empty supported_interfaces list; content is author-supplied.

entries.requirement: The `supportedInterfaces` field **SHOULD** declare all supported protocol combinations in preference order
entries.notes: No derivation or cross-check of the card's interfaces against the dispatchers actually mounted.

entries.requirement: Each interface **MUST** accurately declare its transport protocol and URL
entries.notes: AgentInterface::jsonrpc/grpc/rest emit the spec spellings JSONRPC/GRPC/HTTP+JSON; URL accuracy is the author's.

entries.requirement: URLs **MAY** be reused if multiple transports are available at the same endpoint
entries.notes: No uniqueness constraint on interface URLs.

entries.requirement: Clients MUST: 1. Parse `supportedInterfaces` if present, and select the first supported transport
entries.notes: from_card applies no binding preference (it passed ClientConfig::default().preferred_bindings = ["JSONRPC"] until 2026-10-12, so a card listing [HTTP+JSON, JSONRPC] got JSONRPC). Among interfaces for protocol major 1 the card's order decides, and build() moves past one it cannot construct, which is what 'first supported' requires. from_card_preferring ranks bindings only when the caller asks it to.

entries.requirement: 2. Prefer earlier entries in the ordered list when multiple options are supported
entries.notes: from_card keeps the card's order, earlier entries first, with the rest as build() fallbacks in that order. from_card_preferring lets a caller who explicitly ranks bindings override the agent's order (a2a-go parity); card order then breaks ties within a rank.

entries.requirement: 3. Use the correct URL for the selected transport
entries.notes: Endpoint taken from the selected AgentInterface; fallback moves endpoint and binding together.

entries.requirement: 4. Set the `tenant` field in every request message to exactly the value declared in the selected `AgentInterface` entry (omit the field if `tenant` is not set in that entry)
entries.notes: Per-request params.tenant overrides the card value (user choice). gRPC/WS round-trip not covered by the e2e test.

entries.requirement: Agent Cards **MAY** be digitally signed using JSON Web Signature (JWS)
entries.notes: ES256 and EdDSA signers (signing feature).

entries.requirement: Before signing, the Agent Card content **MUST** be canonicalized using the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) as defined in RFC 8785.
entries.notes: JCS itself is implemented and vector-tested; see 2022/2026 for the pre-canonicalization default-stripping it is fed without.

entries.requirement: Before canonicalization, the JSON representation **MUST** respect Protocol Buffer field presence semantics as defined in Section 5.7.
entries.notes: signing::presence::prune applies protobuf field presence from a table the test checks against the vendored proto.

entries.requirement: Optional fields not explicitly set **MUST** be omitted from the JSON object
entries.notes: `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` on streaming/pushNotifications/extendedAgentCard/documentationUrl/iconUrl; no test asserts absence in canonical bytes.

entries.requirement: Optional fields explicitly set to defaults **MUST** be included in the JSON object
entries.notes: Option<bool> Some(false) serializes `false`; no test pins the spec example's `"pushNotifications":false,"streaming":false` in canonical output.

entries.requirement: Required fields: Fields marked with `REQUIRED` **MUST** always be present, even if the field value matches the default.
entries.notes: name/description/version are String and supportedInterfaces/defaultInput/OutputModes/skills/tags are Vec with no skip_serializing_if, so always present; no test asserts e.g. `"description":""` / `"skills":[]` survive canonicalization.

entries.requirement: Default values: Fields with default values **MUST** be omitted unless the field is marked as `REQUIRED` or has the `optional` keyword.
test_evidence: itk/interop/card_signature_interop.py implicit fields at their defaults
entries.notes: Fixed; interop with the official Python SDK proven both ways (itk/interop/card_signature_interop.py).

entries.requirement: (example table) `extensions`: [] - repeated field (not REQUIRED) with empty array → **omit**; expected canonical {"capabilities":{"pushNotifications":false,"streaming":false},"description":"","name":"Example Agent","skills":[]}
entries.notes: A received `"extensions": []` deserializes to Some(vec![]) and is re-serialized as `"extensions":[]`, so the spec's own worked example canonicalizes differently from the documented output; no test runs the §8.4.1 example.

entries.requirement: The `signatures` field itself **MUST** be excluded from the content being signed to avoid circular dependencies.
The protected header **MUST** include: `alg`
The protected header **MUST** include: ... `kid`: Key ID for identifying the signing key
entries.notes: sign_card_es256/sign_card_ed25519 take the kid as &str. The deprecated sign_agent_card(_ed25519) still accept None until removal (STABILITY.md section 3).

entries.requirement: `typ`: **SHOULD** be set to "JOSE" for JWS
entries.notes: Protected header built as `json!({"alg": "ES256"})` (+kid); `typ` is never emitted by either signer.

entries.requirement: The protected header **MAY** include: `jku`
entries.notes: Signers take no jku parameter; signature_header reads jku from foreign signatures.

entries.requirement: Clients verifying Agent Card signatures MUST: 1. Extract the signature from the `signatures` array
entries.notes: verify_card_with_jwks iterates card.signatures.

entries.requirement: 2. Retrieve the public key using the `kid` and `jku` (or from a trusted key store)
entries.notes: kid-based lookup in a caller-supplied JWKS is implemented and tested; jku is decoded but never followed (deliberately: fetch_jwks takes a caller-trusted URL), so jku retrieval is left to the application.

entries.requirement: 3. Remove properties with default values from the received Agent Card
test_evidence: itk/interop/card_signature_interop.py implicit fields at their defaults
entries.notes: Verification shares canonicalize_card, so it applies the same presence rules.

entries.requirement: 4. Exclude the `signatures` field
5. Canonicalize the resulting JSON using RFC 8785
6. Verify the signature against the canonicalized payload
Clients **SHOULD** verify at least one signature before trusting an Agent Card
entries.notes: resolve_agent_card / ClientBuilder::from_card never verify; the caller must call verify_card_with_jwks (no opt-in verification on the discovery path).

entries.requirement: Public keys **SHOULD** be retrieved over secure channels (HTTPS)
entries.notes: https:// or loopback http:// only.

entries.requirement: Clients **MAY** maintain a trusted key store for known agent providers
entries.notes: Caller-supplied Jwks.

entries.requirement: Expired or revoked keys **MUST NOT** be used for verification
entries.notes: Documented as the caller's obligation; no expiry/revocation check in the SDK (revocation only by removal from the JWKS).

entries.requirement: Multiple signatures **MAY** be present to support key rotation
Servers and clients **SHOULD** use standard HTTP caching mechanisms to reduce unnecessary network overhead.
entries.notes: Server: the public card is cacheable on JSON-RPC, REST and axum, the extended card revalidates (private, no-cache, ETag). Client: CachingCardResolver revalidates; resolve_agent_card and fetch_card_from_url do no caching, and nothing honours max-age or no-store (see 2235).

entries.requirement: Agent Card HTTP endpoints **SHOULD** include a `Cache-Control` response header with a `max-age` directive appropriate for the agent's expected update frequency
entries.notes: JSON-RPC, REST and (since 2026-10-11) the axum router serve the public card with Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 from StaticAgentCardHandler. The max-age is set on StaticAgentCardHandler::with_max_age; the dispatchers build theirs with the default and do not expose it. The axum test fails without the fix (no cache-control).

entries.requirement: Agent Card HTTP endpoints **SHOULD** include an `ETag` response header derived from the Agent Card's `version` field or a hash of the card content
entries.notes: Content-hash ETag (and Last-Modified) on all three HTTP card routes; If-None-Match answers 304. The axum route had neither until 2026-10-11.

entries.requirement: Agent Card HTTP endpoints **MAY** include a `Last-Modified` response header
entries.notes: Set to handler construction time (changes on every restart); If-Modified-Since compared by exact string equality (caching.rs:127).

entries.requirement: Clients **SHOULD** honor HTTP caching semantics as defined in RFC 9111 when fetching Agent Cards
entries.notes: CachingCardResolver revalidates every resolve with the stored validators (permitted by RFC 9111: a cache may always validate) and, since 2026-10-12, does not store a no-store response (RFC 9111 §5.2.2.5), nor one with no validator to revalidate by. Remaining: max-age freshness is not used to skip the request (by choice, so hot-reloaded cards are seen at once), and resolve_agent_card / fetch_card_from_url do no caching.

entries.requirement: When a cached Agent Card has expired, clients **SHOULD** use conditional requests (`If-None-Match` with the stored `ETag`, or `If-Modified-Since`)
entries.notes: CachingCardResolver revalidates on every resolve with If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since from the cached response; a server that answers 304 only to a request carrying both validators sees them on the second fetch. Shown to fail with the If-None-Match header removed.

entries.requirement: When the server does not include caching headers, clients **MAY** apply an implementation-specific default cache duration
entries.notes: No freshness lifetime; every resolve() hits the network.

entries.requirement: Content-Type: `application/json` for requests and responses
entries.notes: Server emits `application/json` (JSON_CONTENT_TYPE) on every JSON-RPC response and accepts application/json or application/a2a+json on ingress; client sends application/json.

entries.requirement: Streaming: Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`); SendStreamingMessage response HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/event-stream, each `data:` a JSON-RPC response echoing the request id
entries.notes: Frames are `id: <seq>\nevent: message\ndata: {jsonrpc,id,result}`; the extra `id:`/`event:` SSE fields are permitted by SSE and do not change the §9.4.2 data shape. Pre-stream errors are returned as plain application/json (deliberate, TCK-driven, jsonrpc/mod.rs:90-97).

entries.requirement: A2A service parameters ... MUST be transmitted using standard HTTP request headers
entries.notes: Server reads A2A-Version/A2A-Extensions/auth from HTTP headers and forwards all headers to the handler; client sets A2A-Version and interceptor-supplied headers as HTTP headers.

entries.requirement: Service parameter names MUST be transmitted as HTTP header fields
entries.notes: Header names are lower-cased by hyper, which satisfies the RFC 7230 case-insensitivity note on line 2257.

entries.requirement: Multiple values for the same service parameter (e.g., A2A-Extensions) SHOULD be comma-separated in a single header field
entries.notes: Client extra_headers is HashMap<String,String> so it can only send one comma-joined field; server splits on commas and echoes activated extensions as one comma-joined field. Robustness note: extract_headers (jsonrpc/response.rs:28, rest/response.rs:21) inserts into a HashMap, so if a peer sends A2A-Extensions as several header lines only the last survives (RFC 9110 allows a recipient to combine them).

entries.requirement: All JSON-RPC requests MUST follow the standard JSON-RPC 2.0 format
entries.notes: `jsonrpc` must be exactly "2.0"; non-JSON answers -32700, JSON that is not a Request answers -32600. Client always emits `jsonrpc:"2.0"`, PascalCase method, params object.

entries.requirement: SubscribeToTask returns UnsupportedOperationError if the task is in a terminal state
entries.notes: Shared handler path, so it holds for JSON-RPC, REST, gRPC, WebSocket and SLIMRPC; wire mapping is -32004 / 400 / FAILED_PRECONDITION (SLIMRPC: UNIMPLEMENTED, see 3025).

entries.requirement: Error Details: Mapped to error.data (array of objects, each containing a @type key, using ProtoJSON Any representation)
entries.notes: Unary errors put an array `[ErrorInfo]` in error.data. The mid-stream JSON-RPC error frame now carries the same typed details as the REST frame (sse.rs error_details): ErrorInfo when the code has an A2A reason, then A2aError.data (the streamLagged marker) as a flat google.protobuf.Struct detail. Until 2026-10-10 it copied A2aError.data through as a bare object. Clients recognise the marker in either shape (A2aError::lag_marker). The WebSocket binding, which is not a spec binding, sends no data at all; see its own entry.

entries.requirement: Standard JSON-RPC error codes -32700/-32600/-32601/-32602/-32603
entries.notes: The codes match the table. The messages are free text such as "Parse error: ..." and "invalid params: ...", not the table's "Standard Message" column. That column is informational, so this is not a violation.

entries.requirement: A2A-specific errors use codes in the range -32001 to -32099 (§5.4 mapping)
entries.notes: A2A errors use -32001..-32099 on every JSON-RPC surface. The WebSocket binding's -32000 (mid-stream and over-capacity) is gone: mid-stream errors keep their own code, and over-capacity is sent as an overload (-32603), as the JSON-RPC HTTP binding sends one.

entries.requirement: Each object in the data array MUST include a @type key that identifies the object's type
entries.notes: Unary/pre-stream: data = [{"@type":"type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo",reason,domain}]. Mid-stream: every element carries @type (ErrorInfo, or google.protobuf.Struct for the streamLagged marker); the server test asserts every element has @type.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD use well-known types such as google.rpc.ErrorInfo ..., or google.rpc.BadRequest to attach structured data to validation errors
entries.notes: A2A errors carry ErrorInfo. Params that do not deserialize answer InvalidParams with a google.rpc.BadRequest naming the field path, on JSON-RPC (HTTP and WebSocket), HTTP+JSON and gRPC (from ConvertError's field).

entries.requirement: Additional error context MAY be included as further objects in the data array
entries.notes: A2aError::data reaches the client as a further detail (a Struct, or as is when it names its @type) on JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON unary responses and on both bindings' stream frames, and on WebSocket. gRPC unary responses carry ErrorInfo, RetryInfo and BadRequest but not arbitrary data.

entries.requirement: A2A service parameters ... MUST be transmitted using gRPC metadata (headers)
entries.notes: Client puts a2a-version plus all interceptor headers into tonic metadata. The server copies ASCII metadata into the header map that the handler reads.

entries.requirement: Service parameter names MUST be transmitted as gRPC metadata keys
entries.notes: Binary (-bin) metadata is skipped on ingress (only KeyAndValueRef::Ascii). That is fine because A2A parameters are ASCII.

entries.requirement: Multiple values for the same service parameter SHOULD be comma-separated in a single metadata entry
