entries.notes: Client can only send one entry per key (HashMap). On ingress, extract_metadata does `map.insert` per entry, so repeated a2a-extensions entries collapse to the last one instead of being joined.

entries.requirement: Implementations MUST extract A2A service parameters from gRPC metadata for processing
entries.notes: All 11 RPCs call validated_metadata(request.metadata(), ..) and pass the headers to the handler.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD validate required service parameters (e.g., A2A-Version) from metadata
entries.notes: Absent, empty or non-1.x versions are rejected with FAILED_PRECONDITION plus ErrorInfo VERSION_NOT_SUPPORTED under the default require_version_header=true.

entries.requirement: For A2A-specific errors, implementations MUST include a google.rpc.ErrorInfo message in the status.details array with reason (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE) and domain "a2a-protocol.org"
entries.notes: Unary and pre-stream errors carry ErrorInfo through tonic_types. Mid-stream, reader_to_native_stream replaces any queue error with `Status::internal("event queue error")` (native.rs:94). Today only InternalError (no reason) reaches that path, so no MUST is broken, but the streamLagged marker and the message are lost there, unlike on SSE.

entries.requirement: Content-Type: application/a2a+json SHOULD be used for requests and responses
entries.notes: Server labels responses application/a2a+json only when Accept prefers it or the request body was a2a+json. Otherwise, including a bare request with no Accept, it sends application/json, so the spec examples at lines 2843-2844 and 2929-2930 are not matched by default. This is a deliberate interop trade-off for a2a-go (media_type.rs:8-25).

entries.requirement: Content-Type: application/a2a+json SHOULD be used for requests
entries.notes: Deliberately not followed, for interop. The REST client sends Content-Type: application/json. a2a-java 1.3.0.Final's REST server refuses any other (A2AServerRoutes.validateContentType: contentType.trim().startsWith("application/json"), else ContentTypeNotSupportedError; read from the jar's bytecode with javap, 2026-10-10), so sending application/a2a+json would break every call to it. a2a-go v2.5.0 and a2a-sdk 1.1.4 servers do not check the request type, and this server accepts both. Revisit when a2a-java accepts application/a2a+json.

entries.requirement: A2A service parameters ... MUST be transmitted using standard HTTP request headers
entries.notes: RestDispatcher validates A2A-Version and forwards headers. The axum adapter (A2aRouter) forwards headers but never calls validate_version_header: rg finds no version check in axum_adapter.rs, so the HTTP+JSON bindings differ on §3.6.2.

entries.requirement: Service parameter names MUST be transmitted as HTTP header fields
Multiple values for the same service parameter SHOULD be comma-separated in a single header field
entries.notes: Same as 2258. Repeated header lines collapse to the last one in rest/response.rs:21.

entries.requirement: REST URL patterns: POST /message:send, /message:stream; GET /tasks/{id}; GET /tasks; POST /tasks/{id}:cancel; POST /tasks/{id}:subscribe; push-config CRUD under /tasks/{id}/pushNotificationConfigs[/{configId}]; GET /extendedAgentCard
entries.notes: Every route exists on server and client, plus tolerated aliases (GET :subscribe, /tasks/{id}/cancel, singular pushNotificationConfig, POST .../{id}/delete). The client percent-encodes path ids; since 2026-10-12 the REST dispatcher decodes task and config ids (and the tenant) after routing, with + literal as RFC 3986 says, and the axum router routes on the raw path before decoding, so an id with a space, +, : or / round-trips on both. Shown to fail with the decoder disabled.

entries.requirement: HTTP methods that do not support request bodies (GET, DELETE) MUST transmit operation request parameters as path parameters or query parameters
entries.notes: Client sends an empty body on GET/DELETE and puts the leftover params in the query. Server reads GetTask historyLength and ListTasks filters from the query, and the tenant from `?tenant=` when there is no path prefix.

entries.requirement: Query parameter names MUST use camelCase to match the JSON serialization of Protocol Buffer field names
entries.notes: Keys used: contextId, status, pageSize, pageToken, statusTimestampAfter, includeArtifacts, historyLength, tenant. Note: a malformed value such as `status=BOGUS` or `pageSize=abc` is silently dropped (`.ok()`) instead of rejected, so the filter is ignored and an unfiltered list is returned.

entries.requirement: Booleans lowercase strings; Numbers decimal strings; Enums string values (status=TASK_STATE_WORKING); Datetimes ISO 8601
entries.notes: Server also accepts `1` for true and legacy lowercase enum aliases. Both are lenient extensions.

entries.requirement: Repeated Fields: multiple values MAY be passed by repeating the parameter name or as comma-separated values
entries.notes: No v1.0 GET/DELETE request has a repeated field, so this has no wire effect today. The client would JSON-encode an array (`ids=%5B1%2C2%2C3%5D`), which matches neither MAY form, and parse_query_param returns only the first occurrence.

entries.requirement: Nested Objects: Not supported in query parameters; operations requiring nested objects MUST use POST with a request body
entries.notes: Every operation with nested fields (SendMessage, CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig, CancelTask metadata) is routed POST, so the MUST holds by route design. build_query_string would still JSON-encode a nested object into the query instead of refusing it (test pins this), which is latent rather than wire-observable.

entries.requirement: All query parameter values MUST be properly URL-encoded per RFC 3986
entries.notes: Client encodes everything except RFC 3986 unreserved chars. Server percent-decodes values (and `+` as space). Query keys are compared undecoded, which is harmless for the camelCase ASCII keys.

entries.requirement: Error Code mapped to the HTTP status code and the error.code field; message to error.message; details to error.details
entries.notes: Body shape `{error:{code,status,message,details}}` matches the spec example at lines 2932-2949, except that ErrorInfo.metadata is never populated (it is optional).

entries.requirement: Each object in the details array MUST include a @type key that identifies the object's type
entries.notes: Unary details = [ErrorInfo]. Stream error frames add a typed google.protobuf.Struct detail for A2aError.data.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD use well-known types such as google.rpc.BadRequest to attach structured data to validation errors
entries.notes: A request body that is valid JSON of the wrong shape answers 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT with a google.rpc.BadRequest detail whose fieldViolation names the path (e.g. message.parts[0].text), on RestDispatcher (send, cancel, subscribe, create push config) and the axum router (send, create push config). Malformed JSON stays a plain 400. Not covered: query-string parameter errors and the JSON-RPC binding's -32602.

entries.requirement: Additional error context MAY be included as further objects in the details array
entries.notes: Unary REST drops A2aError.data (`error_info_data(None)`). Only the SSE error frame forwards it, as a Struct detail.

entries.requirement: implementations MUST include a google.rpc.ErrorInfo object in the details array for A2A-specific errors with @type, reason, domain
entries.notes: ContentTypeNotSupportedError now goes through server_error_to_response with its ErrorInfo on REST and axum.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD avoid re-ordering events
entries.notes: A single ordered per-task queue drives SSE, gRPC, WebSocket and SLIMRPC streams. REST frames are bare StreamResponse objects as the §11.7 example requires.

entries.requirement: MAY optionally resend a final Task snapshot before closing
entries.notes: No code appends a final Task snapshot; the stream simply ends after the terminal/interrupted event.

entries.requirement: implementers MAY create custom protocol bindings
entries.notes: Two custom bindings: WebSocket (https://a2a-rust.com/bindings/websocket/v1) and SLIMRPC (https://a2a-protocol.org/bindings/experimental-slimrpc/v1).

entries.requirement: Custom bindings MUST comply with all requirements defined in Section 5
entries.notes: SLIMRPC sends PushNotificationNotSupported and UnsupportedOperation as UNIMPLEMENTED where A2A §5.4's gRPC column says FAILED_PRECONDITION. This is the SLIMRPC spec's own §6.1 'canonical mapping' (a MUST), which the binding now follows exactly; the conflict is between the two specifications, not an implementation defect, and is left PARTIAL until upstream resolves it. The stale 'identical to dispatch/grpc' comment was rewritten.

entries.requirement: Custom protocol bindings MUST: 1. Implement All Core Operations
entries.notes: Both bindings route all 11 v1.0 methods to the shared RequestHandler. WebSocket also accepts the v0.3 alias `message/stream` (websocket.rs:883). The module rustdoc (websocket.rs:20-23) says v0.3 names are rejected, while the book (dispatchers.md:225-229) documents the alias; the alias is untested (ws_legacy_method_names_rejected covers only message/send, tasks/list, tasks/get).

entries.requirement: 2. Preserve Data Model: Use data structures functionally equivalent to those defined in Section 4
entries.notes: WebSocket reuses the JSON-RPC ProtoJSON types. SLIMRPC uses the canonical lf.a2a.v1 protobuf messages.

entries.requirement: 3. Maintain Semantics: Ensure operations behave consistently with the abstract operation definitions
entries.notes: Same handler, so the semantics match. Deviations: WebSocket ends every stream with a synthetic success frame `{"result":{"status":"stream_complete"}}` that is not a StreamResponse (documented). SLIMRPC accepts a missing a2a-version (methods/mod.rs:96 `validate_version_metadata(&headers, false)`), unlike the strict default of the other bindings. Its rationale comment ("the gRPC binding already made exactly this trade") is stale, since gRPC now enforces it (helpers.rs:42-51).

entries.requirement: 4. Document Completely: Provide comprehensive documentation of the binding specification
entries.notes: WebSocket now has a binding specification (book/src/bindings/websocket.md): connection, service parameters, messages, data types, streaming, errors, authentication, security, differences from JSON-RPC over HTTP. SLIMRPC follows the vendored upstream spec. The page's wire claims are pinned by websocket_binding_spec.rs (handshake refusal and query fallback, refusal codes and ErrorInfo, stream frames and marker), which passed against the page as written.

entries.requirement: Custom bindings MUST provide clear mappings for: Protocol Buffer Types, Timestamps, Binary Data, Enumerations
entries.notes: WebSocket spec §3 'Data types' states the ProtoJSON mappings: lowerCamelCase names, enum names as strings, RFC 3339 UTC timestamps, base64 bytes, Struct as JSON object; binary frames refused. SLIMRPC is protobuf on the wire.

entries.requirement: custom protocol bindings MUST document how service parameters are transmitted ... MUST address: Transmission Mechanism, Value Constraints, Reserved Names, Fallback Strategy
entries.notes: WebSocket spec §2 covers transmission, value constraints, reserved names (:path) and fallback (A2A-Version query parameter only). The page's wire claims are pinned by websocket_binding_spec.rs (handshake refusal and query fallback, refusal codes and ErrorInfo, stream frames and marker), which passed against the page as written.

entries.requirement: Transmission Mechanism (SLIMRPC: service parameter keys are case-insensitive in metadata, spec/slimrpc_v1/slimrpc.md:63)
entries.notes: a2a_headers lowercases every key after filtering the transport keys, so the handler's lowercase lookups (authorization, a2a-extensions, a2a-version, tenant headers) see a capitalised key; keys differing only in case are joined with ', '. Until 2026-10-10 keys kept the peer's case and were ignored.

entries.requirement: Custom bindings MUST: 1. Map Standard Errors: Provide mappings for all A2A-specific error types
2. Preserve Error Information: Ensure error details are accessible to clients
entries.notes: WebSocket: unary, mid-stream and over-capacity errors now carry their own code and the same typed data array as the JSON-RPC HTTP binding (ErrorInfo, RetryInfo, BadRequest, A2aError::data); mid-stream errors keep their A2A code and the streamLagged marker instead of -32000. Remaining (why PARTIAL/low): SLIMRPC keeps identity through its TypeNameError: message prefix but carries no details, as its spec defines no details encoding.

entries.requirement: 3. Use Appropriate Codes: Map to protocol-native error codes where applicable
entries.notes: The binding follows the SLIMRPC spec's §6.1 table row by row (ParseError INTERNAL, ContentTypeNotSupported/Push/UnsupportedOperation UNIMPLEMENTED) and A2A §5.4's gRPC code for the three errors the table omits (FAILED_PRECONDITION). The table's UNKNOWN row has no case to apply to: every ServerError converts to an A2A code. Where the SLIMRPC table and A2A §5.4's gRPC column disagree (Push, UnsupportedOperation), the binding's own table is followed; see the §12 entry at line 2985.

entries.requirement: 4. Document Error Format: Specify the structure of error responses
entries.notes: WebSocket spec §1 and §5 document the handshake error body and the JSON-RPC error object with its typed data array, with a code table for every A2A error. The page's wire claims are pinned by websocket_binding_spec.rs (handshake refusal and query fallback, refusal codes and ErrorInfo, stream frames and marker), which passed against the page as written.

entries.requirement: Define Stream Mechanism; Event Ordering; Reconnection; Stream Termination
entries.notes: WebSocket spec §4: mechanism (frames carrying the request id), ordering (per stream in production order; streams on one connection interleave), reconnection (none; resubscribe, first event is the snapshot), termination (stream_complete marker, or an error frame). The page's wire claims are pinned by websocket_binding_spec.rs (handshake refusal and query fallback, refusal codes and ErrorInfo, stream frames and marker), which passed against the page as written.

entries.requirement: If streaming is not supported, the binding MUST clearly document this limitation in the Agent Card
entries.notes: Both custom bindings support streaming.

entries.requirement: Custom bindings MUST: Support Standard Schemes; Document Integration; Handle Challenges; Maintain Security
entries.notes: WebSocket spec §6 documents integration: credentials on the upgrade headers, checked per request; a refused credential is -32600 in the body with no 401/WWW-Authenticate (the connection is already upgraded), and browsers cannot set Authorization. Remaining: no in-band challenge, which the binding cannot send; the documented workaround is a gateway. SLIMRPC authenticates at the transport and maps refusals to UNAUTHENTICATED/PERMISSION_DENIED.

entries.requirement: Custom bindings MUST be declared in the Agent Card (URI transport identifier + full endpoint URL) - WebSocket
entries.notes: The SDK provides the URI constant WEBSOCKET_BINDING_URI and AgentInterface::new(url, uri). WebSocketDispatcher never adds itself to the card, so the agent author must.

entries.requirement: Custom bindings MUST be declared in the Agent Card (URI transport identifier + full endpoint URL) - SLIMRPC
entries.notes: server.agent_interface() builds the interface with the upstream URI. The application must still push it onto card.supported_interfaces (README example).

entries.requirement: Custom binding implementers SHOULD: Test Against Reference; Document Differences; Provide Examples; Test Edge Cases
entries.notes: WebSocket: examples and a differences table are in the binding spec (§3, §5, §8); TCK --equivalence compares it with the spec bindings; edge cases are tested in websocket.rs and websocket_*.rs. SLIMRPC is checked against upstream's spec and the official crate.

entries.requirement: Implementations MUST ensure appropriate scope limitation based on the authenticated caller's authorization boundaries. This applies to all operations that access or list tasks and other resources.
entries.notes: With RequestHandlerBuilder::isolate_tasks_by_caller the authenticated caller's identity selects the store partition (TenantContext::partition), so another caller's task is TaskNotFound like an unknown id and lists hold only the caller's own; the SDK enforces it, the agent author turns it on (off by default: sharing within a tenant stays the default). Shared-access models (roles, groups) map the group to a tenant with a TenantResolver. Before this branch: The only scoping the SDK performs is the tenant partition (TenantContext task-local + TenantAware* stores, resolver-derived tenant). Within a tenant (and in the default single-tenant deployment) there is no principal scoping and no hook to add one: TaskStore::get/list take only the id/params, CallContext carries no task id or params, and the authenticated caller_identity is not visible to the store; the only workaround is to make each principal a tenant via a credential-verifying TenantResolver.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST implement authorization checks on every A2A Protocol Operations request
entries.notes: SDK hook provided: every handler entry point (all 11 operations, all bindings incl. WebSocket per message) runs ServerInterceptorChain::before, and ServerInterceptor can return A2aError::permission_denied keyed on ctx.method()/caller_identity(). Nothing enforces that an authorizer is registered; a default build performs no authorization (the interceptor sees no task id, so per-resource checks cannot be written there; see 3100).

entries.requirement: Implementations MUST scope results to the caller's authorized access boundaries as defined by the agent's authorization model
entries.notes: With RequestHandlerBuilder::isolate_tasks_by_caller the authenticated caller's identity selects the store partition (TenantContext::partition), so another caller's task is TaskNotFound like an unknown id and lists hold only the caller's own; the SDK enforces it, the agent author turns it on (off by default: sharing within a tenant stays the default). Shared-access models (roles, groups) map the group to a tenant with a TenantResolver. Before this branch: Tenant-boundary models are supported (store partition chosen by TenantContext::scope); user/role/project models within a tenant are not: `self.task_store.list(&params)` receives no caller, and there is no post-filter hook between store and response.

entries.requirement: Even when contextId or other filter parameters are not specified in requests, implementations MUST scope results to the caller's authorized access boundaries
entries.notes: With RequestHandlerBuilder::isolate_tasks_by_caller the authenticated caller's identity selects the store partition (TenantContext::partition), so another caller's task is TaskNotFound like an unknown id and lists hold only the caller's own; the SDK enforces it, the agent author turns it on (off by default: sharing within a tenant stays the default). Shared-access models (roles, groups) map the group to a tenant with a TenantResolver. Before this branch: An unfiltered ListTasks (ListTasksParams::default()) is scoped to the tenant partition only; any authenticated caller in the same/default tenant gets every task in it.

entries.requirement: Authorization models are agent-defined and MAY be based on: user identity, roles/groups, project/workspace, tenant boundaries, custom logic
entries.notes: MAY: multi-tenant model SUPPORTED (TenantResolver + TenantAware stores); user/role/project models only expressible as tenants or as method-level allow/deny in an interceptor; no resource-level hook. (Re-graded on 2026-10-10: a MAY takes SUPPORTED/NOT_SUPPORTED; the tenant model is supported, and the missing per-principal hook is the §13.1 entries at lines 3083-3101.) The user-identity model is now supported too: isolate_tasks_by_caller.

entries.requirement: List Tasks: MUST only return tasks visible to the authenticated client according to the agent's authorization model
entries.notes: With RequestHandlerBuilder::isolate_tasks_by_caller the authenticated caller's identity selects the store partition (TenantContext::partition), so another caller's task is TaskNotFound like an unknown id and lists hold only the caller's own; the SDK enforces it, the agent author turns it on (off by default: sharing within a tenant stays the default). Shared-access models (roles, groups) map the group to a tenant with a TenantResolver. Before this branch: Tenant-scoped only (store-level tests, no handler/wire-level cross-tenant ListTasks test found). No way to restrict visibility per principal inside a tenant: two callers authenticated by BearerTokenAuthInterceptor::with_labelled_tokens in the default tenant see each other's tasks.

entries.requirement: Get Task: MUST verify the authenticated client has access to the requested task according to the agent's authorization model
entries.notes: With RequestHandlerBuilder::isolate_tasks_by_caller the authenticated caller's identity selects the store partition (TenantContext::partition), so another caller's task is TaskNotFound like an unknown id and lists hold only the caller's own; the SDK enforces it, the agent author turns it on (off by default: sharing within a tenant stays the default). Shared-access models (roles, groups) map the group to a tenant with a TenantResolver. Before this branch: A task in another tenant partition is TaskNotFound (good, no existence leak). Within a partition, `self.task_store.get(&task_id)` is returned to any caller who passed the interceptor chain; the interceptor cannot see params.id (CallContext has method/headers/identity/tenant only), so a per-task access check has no SDK hook.

entries.requirement: Task-related operations (Cancel, Subscribe, Push Notification Config): MUST verify the client has appropriate access rights according to the agent's authorization model
entries.notes: With RequestHandlerBuilder::isolate_tasks_by_caller the authenticated caller's identity selects the store partition (TenantContext::partition), so another caller's task is TaskNotFound like an unknown id and lists hold only the caller's own; the SDK enforces it, the agent author turns it on (off by default: sharing within a tenant stays the default). Shared-access models (roles, groups) map the group to a tenant with a TenantResolver. Before this branch: Same as GetTask: tenant partition enforced for cancel/subscribe/push-config CRUD; no per-principal ownership check (any caller in the partition can cancel, subscribe to, or register a webhook on another caller's task).

entries.requirement: Authorization checks MUST occur before any database queries or operations that could leak information about the existence of resources outside the caller's authorization scope
entries.notes: call.before() (interceptors) and resolve_tenant/isolatable run before any task_store access in every handler; out-of-partition tasks surface as TaskNotFound, indistinguishable from nonexistent. Caveat: the CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig taskId-empty check (push_config.rs:167) runs before interceptors but reads no store.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD document their authorization model and access control policies
entries.notes: Deployment documentation duty; the SDK documents its own (tenant-only) model in tenant_resolver.rs module docs and book/src/deployment/multi-tenancy.md.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST include authentication credentials in webhook requests as specified in PushNotificationConfig.authentication
entries.notes: The sender writes Authorization for Bearer and Basic (case-insensitive), as a2a-go v2.5.0 does. A config naming any other scheme is now refused at creation with InvalidParams, so no webhook is called without the credentials its config specifies. Until 2026-10-10 such a config was stored and delivered without credentials (a2a-go still does that). The sender's runtime drop remains for configs stored before.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement reasonable timeout values for webhook requests (recommended: 10-30 seconds)
entries.notes: HttpPushSender's per-request timeout is 30s, but HandlerLimits::push_delivery_timeout defaults to 5s and wraps the whole send, so the effective default webhook timeout is 5s, below the recommended 10-30s (configurable). A test pins the contradiction.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement retry logic with exponential backoff for failed deliveries
entries.notes: 3 attempts, backoff [1s,2s] (doubling; schedule is an explicit list whose last entry repeats, not computed exponential). Retries 5xx/408/429/transport errors only. Caveat: under the default 5s handler bound a timed-out first attempt leaves no time for retries (see 3118).

entries.requirement: Agents MAY stop attempting delivery after a configured number of consecutive failures
entries.notes: Per-event max_attempts only; no cross-event circuit breaker that disables a config after N consecutive failed events.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD validate webhook URLs to prevent SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery) attacks
entries.notes: Synchronous host check at config creation, DNS-resolve-all + IP pinning at delivery (http), cert validation defeats rebinding for https. Bypassable only by explicit HttpPushSender::allow_private_urls().
Also CGNAT, 0.0.0.0, IPv6 ULA, IPv4-mapped/NAT64 forms and inet_aton numeric encodings.

entries.requirement: Reject localhost and link-local addresses
entries.notes: localhost, *.local, *.internal hostnames and 169.254/16, fe80::/10 rejected.

entries.requirement: Implement URL allowlists where appropriate
entries.notes: Opt-in HttpPushSender::with_allowed_hosts: exact host match, ignoring case and port, no wildcards. Enforced at config creation (InvalidParams) and again at delivery before any connection. Custom senders can answer PushSender::allows_webhook_url (default true).

entries.requirement: Clients MUST validate webhook authenticity using the provided authentication credentials
entries.notes: No webhook receiver exists in the client crate (no 'webhook' in a2a-protocol-client/src). The server crate offers only push::webhook::notification_token() to extract the token; the receiver must validate it (and Authorization) itself.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD verify the task ID in the payload matches an expected task they created
entries.notes: No receiver-side helper; application duty.

entries.requirement: Clients MUST respond with HTTP 2xx status codes to acknowledge successful receipt
entries.notes: Receiver duty; the SDK sender side treats any 2xx (`resp.status().is_success()`) as delivered, consistent with this.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD process notifications idempotently, as duplicate deliveries may occur
entries.notes: Receiver duty; no SDK receiver.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD implement rate limiting to prevent webhook flooding
entries.notes: Receiver duty; no SDK receiver.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD use HTTPS endpoints for webhook URLs to ensure confidentiality
entries.notes: Client picks the URL; the A2A client does not warn on http:// push URLs and the server accepts both http and https.

entries.requirement: Webhook URLs SHOULD use HTTPS to protect payload confidentiality in transit
entries.notes: HTTPS delivery supported (tls-rustls feature, on by default via sdk); plain http also accepted with no warning or opt-in. No test or option enforcing https-only.

entries.requirement: Authentication tokens in TaskPushNotificationConfig SHOULD be treated as secrets and rotated periodically
entries.notes: Secret handling (Debug redaction, origin-only URL logging) tested; rotation is an application duty (re-create config).

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD securely store push notification configurations and credentials
entries.notes: SQL push-config stores persist the whole config (incl. authentication.credentials and token) as plaintext JSON (`serde_json::to_string(&config)`); no at-rest encryption hook. In-memory and Debug output are redacted.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD use unique, single-purpose tokens for each push notification configuration
entries.notes: Client application choice; SDK neither generates nor checks token uniqueness.

entries.requirement: The Get Extended Agent Card operation MUST require authentication
entries.notes: Refused unless an interceptor reporting authenticates()==true is registered, or the operator opts out with allow_unauthenticated_extended_card(). Note: the 'extended' card served is a clone of the same handler.agent_card that the dispatchers publish at /.well-known/agent-card.json (rest/mod.rs:63), so there is no way to serve a distinct extended card.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST authenticate requests using one of the schemes declared in the public AgentCard.securitySchemes and AgentCard.security fields
entries.notes: No cross-check between the registered auth interceptor(s) and card.security_schemes/security_requirements (grep for security_schemes in server src finds nothing outside tests); keeping them consistent is on the operator.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY return different extended card content based on the authenticated client's identity or authorization level
entries.notes: extended_card_for_this_call returns `card.clone()` of the single configured card; no per-caller card provider hook.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement appropriate caching headers to control client-side caching of extended cards
entries.notes: GET /extendedAgentCard (RestDispatcher and the axum router) sends Cache-Control: private, no-cache, Vary: Authorization and an ETag over the serialized card, and answers 304 to a matching If-None-Match. JSON-RPC, gRPC and WebSocket fetch the card over POST or a stream, where HTTP caching headers do not apply.

entries.requirement: Extended cards MAY include additional skills not present in the public card
entries.notes: Public and extended card are the same handler.agent_card.

entries.requirement: Extended cards MAY expose more detailed capability information (e.g., rate limits, quotas)
entries.notes: Same single card.

entries.requirement: Extended cards MAY include organization-specific or user-specific configuration
entries.notes: Same single card, no per-caller variation.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD document which capabilities are available at different authentication levels
entries.notes: Operator documentation duty.

entries.requirement: Extended cards SHOULD NOT include sensitive information that could be exploited if leaked (e.g., internal service URLs, unmasked credentials)
entries.notes: Card content is operator-authored; since the SDK's extended card equals the public card, it adds nothing sensitive itself.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST validate that clients have appropriate permissions before returning privileged information in extended cards
entries.notes: Interceptor chain runs before the card is produced (method-level permission check possible via ctx.method()=='GetExtendedAgentCard'). The SDK cannot serve privileged content distinct from the public card, so in practice nothing privileged is returned.

entries.requirement: Clients retrieving extended cards SHOULD replace their cached public Agent Card with the extended version for the duration of their authenticated session
entries.notes: CachingCardResolver::install_extended_card serves the extended card from resolve() without fetching until clear_extended_card() or invalidate(). The application still decides when the session starts and ends; A2aClient keeps no card of its own.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD version extended cards appropriately and honor client cache invalidation
entries.notes: card.version stays operator-set. Cache invalidation is honoured through revalidation: no-cache makes the client check every use, and the ETag changes whenever the card does (a new version included, tested), so a stale cached card is replaced on the next request.

entries.requirement: When capabilities.extendedAgentCard is false or not present, the operation MUST return UnsupportedOperationError
entries.notes: Correct when the handler has a card with the flag false/absent. When the handler has no card at all (capability therefore not declared by this handler) it returns ExtendedAgentCardNotConfigured instead of UnsupportedOperationError; a test asserts that ordering.

entries.requirement: When support is declared but no extended card is configured, the operation MUST return ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError
entries.notes: Reachable only when no card is given to the handler (e.g. public card served separately). If the handler's card declares the flag, that same card is served as the 'extended' card, so the not-configured state cannot arise.

entries.requirement: Production deployments MUST use encrypted communication (HTTPS for HTTP-based bindings, TLS for gRPC)
entries.notes: Client: rustls HTTPS on by default (tls-rustls), grpc-tls feature. Server: gRPC TLS via GrpcDispatcher::with_tls (grpc-tls); the built-in hyper serve()/WebSocket listeners are plaintext only, so HTTPS for JSON-RPC/REST/WS requires an external terminator or the axum adapter with the operator's own TLS. Deployment duty.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD use modern TLS configurations (TLS 1.3+ recommended) with strong cipher suites
entries.notes: rustls 0.23.45 implements only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 (its versions.rs defines no other SupportedProtocolVersion), so SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0/1.1 cannot be offered. The client's config negotiates TLS 1.3 with a server that has it and enables only forward-secret AEAD suites (TLS13_* and TLS_ECDHE_*_GCM/CHACHA20_POLY1305); shown to fail with the client limited to TLS 1.2. TLS 1.2 stays enabled for peers without 1.3. The push sender's default config (push/sender.rs) uses the same builder chain; it is read, not handshake-tested.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD enforce HSTS (HTTP Strict Transport Security) headers when using HTTP-based bindings
entries.notes: Opt-in dispatch::Hsts wraps any Dispatcher and sets Strict-Transport-Security on every response, errors included. The built-in listener is plaintext and browsers ignore HSTS over plain HTTP (RFC 6797 §8.1), so it takes effect behind a TLS terminator; axum users add it with their own middleware. Not on by default: a header claiming HTTPS on a plaintext deployment would be wrong.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD disable support for deprecated SSL/TLS versions (SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1)
entries.notes: rustls 0.23.45 implements only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 (its versions.rs defines no other SupportedProtocolVersion), so SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0/1.1 cannot be offered. The client's config negotiates TLS 1.3 with a server that has it and enables only forward-secret AEAD suites (TLS13_* and TLS_ECDHE_*_GCM/CHACHA20_POLY1305); shown to fail with the client limited to TLS 1.2. TLS 1.2 stays enabled for peers without 1.3. The push sender's default config (push/sender.rs) uses the same builder chain; it is read, not handshake-tested.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST validate all input parameters before processing
entries.notes: Protocol-level validation (ids, metadata size, timestamps, page size clamp, push URL) in the SDK; validation of message content semantics is the executor's. Detailed per-field validation is covered by other sections' audits.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement appropriate limits on message sizes, file sizes, and request complexity
entries.notes: Body cap (4 MiB default), gRPC message cap, WS frame cap, metadata/id/parts/artifacts caps.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD sanitize or validate file content types and reject unexpected media types
entries.notes: Part mediaType checked against card defaultInputModes/skill inputModes; parts without mediaType and content sniffing are not checked (content sanitization is the executor's).

entries.requirement: API keys, tokens, and other credentials MUST be treated as secrets
entries.notes: Constant-time comparison, Debug shows counts not keys, identity labels separate from credentials, push secrets redacted. Exception: SQL push-config stores keep credentials plaintext at rest (see 3139).

entries.requirement: Credentials SHOULD be rotated periodically
entries.notes: JWKS remote key sets support key rotation; client token providers refresh. Static allow-lists are fixed at construction.

entries.requirement: Credentials SHOULD be transmitted only over encrypted connections
entries.notes: Neither client auth interceptors nor the push sender refuse to send credentials over http://; deployment choice.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement credential revocation mechanisms
entries.notes: No revocation API (no jti/deny-list in jwt.rs; static key/token lists immutable after construction); revocation via JWKS key removal/expiry or a custom interceptor.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD log authentication failures
entries.notes: With the `audit` feature + with_audit, refused calls are recorded (test sends a credential-less call and asserts a record with no actor). The auth interceptors themselves emit no log line; metrics on_error counts failures.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement rate limiting to prevent brute-force attacks
entries.notes: RateLimitInterceptor limits throughput per caller, but nothing throttles failed authentication: the docs say to register the limiter after the auth interceptor (so it can key by identity), and a refused credential never reaches it. Registering it first keys unauthenticated callers by trusted x-forwarded-for hops or one shared 'anonymous' bucket, which lets one attacker exhaust everyone's budget. Per-source throttling of auth failures needs the peer address, which CallContext does not carry. Recorded for the maintainer: plumb the peer address into CallContext and count auth failures per source.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD log security-relevant events (authentication failures, authorization denials, suspicious requests)
entries.notes: Opt-in audit feature records every call with outcome.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement monitoring for unusual patterns (rapid task creation, excessive cancellations)
entries.notes: SDK exposes Metrics (on_request/on_error/on_latency per method) and OTel; anomaly detection is the operator's.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD provide audit trails for sensitive operations
entries.notes: Hash-chained per-tenant audit log (feature `audit`, opt-in).

entries.requirement: Logs MUST NOT include sensitive information (credentials, personal data) unless required and properly protected
entries.notes: Message content capture in spans defaults off (SpanSettings.content=false); audit records digests not content.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement rate limiting on all operations
entries.notes: Opt-in interceptor; applies to every operation since the chain runs on all handlers.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD return appropriate error responses when rate limits are exceeded
entries.notes: RateLimitInterceptor refuses with A2aError::rate_limited, retrying when the window ends: HTTP+JSON 429 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED with Retry-After, gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, and a google.rpc.RetryInfo detail on every binding. The JSON-RPC code stays -32603, the code §3.3.2 (spec line 536) gives as its example for 'rate limit exceeded'. Until 2026-10-10 the refusal was a plain internal error (500 / INTERNAL), indistinguishable from a server fault. The WebSocket binding sends no error data, so its callers see only -32603.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY implement different rate limits for different operations or user tiers
entries.notes: Per-tenant allowance (tiers via tenant config) supported; no per-operation limits in the built-in limiter (custom interceptor can key on ctx.method()).

entries.requirement: Agents MUST comply with applicable data protection regulations
entries.notes: Legal/operational duty; not SDK-testable.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD provide mechanisms for users to request deletion of their data
entries.notes: TaskStore::delete exists; no A2A operation or per-user deletion API (no per-user ownership, see 3083).

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement appropriate data retention policies
entries.notes: In-memory TTL default 1h; persistent stores keep everything unless purge_expired is configured (documented decision); audit has its own retention.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD minimize logging of sensitive or personal information
entries.notes: Span content capture off by default; webhook URLs logged as origin only.

entries.requirement: Custom protocol bindings MUST address security considerations in their specification
entries.notes: WebSocket spec §7 addresses transport (ws:// only; TLS terminator), the unchecked Origin header and cross-site WebSocket hijacking where credentials are ambient, one identity per connection, and limits. SLIMRPC follows its upstream binding spec. Recorded for the maintainer: an opt-in Origin allowlist on the dispatcher.

entries.requirement: Custom bindings SHOULD follow the same security principles as standard bindings
entries.notes: WebSocket routes through the same RequestHandler, so interceptors (auth, rate limit, audit) and tenant resolution apply identically per message.

entries.requirement: Custom bindings MUST document authentication integration and credential transmission
impl_evidence: book/src/concepts/transport-layers.md:188 (WebSocket: credentials at connect as upgrade headers)
book/src/bindings/slimrpc.md (SLIMRPC: credentials as session metadata; transport identity)
entries.notes: Documentation requirement. WebSocket: credentials ride the upgrade request's headers. SLIMRPC: since 2026-10-11 the book says per-call headers (authorization included) become session metadata of the same name, lowercased by the server and read as request headers, as the code does (client metadata_from, server a2a_headers, read 2026-10-11). No test checks documentation. No standalone document at the WebSocket binding URI.

entries.notes: Linter directive naming a rule; no normative content.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD use this to tailor their output.
entries.notes: RequestContext::accepted_output_modes() now carries SendMessageConfiguration.acceptedOutputModes to the executor (empty = no preference); tailoring the output is the agent's job. Until 2026-10-10 the executor could not see the field at all.

entries.notes: Server is tolerant: it overwrites the inline config's task_id with the created task (`task_id: Some(task_id.0.clone()), ..inline`). Client does not clear a caller-set taskId (lowercase 'should', client-side, harmless given server override).

entries.requirement: The server MUST NOT return more messages than the provided value
entries.notes: shape_response_history -> truncate_history keeps the last n; n=0 omits history; absent omits history entirely (a lower limit, permitted).

entries.requirement: but MAY apply a lower limit.
